```python
# You can specify HTTPS as the protocol:
# request.set_protocol_type('https')
######
request.set_accept_format('json') request.set_method('POST') request.add_query_param('PageNumber','1') request.add_query_param('PageSize','30')
######
# When you use an STS AccessKey 3-tuple to call an API operation, you must add the SecurityToken field in the request parameters.
# Format:
# Specify your security token.
# request.add_query_param("SecurityToken", "<yourSecurityToken>");
######
# Optional. Specify the resource set ID.
request.add_header("x-acs-resourcegroupid", "<yourResourceGroupID>")
# Required. Specify the organization ID.
request.add_header("x-acs-organizationid", "<yourOrganizationID>")
# Required. Specify the source of the API call.
request.add_header("x-acs-caller-sdk-source","ApiTestDemo")
# Optional. Specify the region ID. If you use Apsara Stack Enterprise V3.15.0 or earlier, this parameter is required.
request.add_header("x-acs-regionid", "<yourRegionID>")
# Optional. Specify the instance ID. If you need to delete, modify, or query an instance, this parameter is required.
# request.add_header("x-acs-instanceid", "<yourInstanceID>")
response = client.do_action_with_exception(request) print(str(response, encoding = 'utf-8'))
```

### 2.4 API Reference

The API operations table lists the API operations that are available for use in Apsara File Storage NAS. Table 1. API operations

| No. | Category | API operation | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Region | DescribeRegions | Queries all region IDs. |
| 2 | File system | CreateFileSystem | Creates a file system. |
| 3 | File system | DeleteFileSystem | Deletes a file system. |
| 4 | File system | DescribeFileSystems | Queries the information of file systems. |
| 5 | File system | ModifyFileSystem | Modifies the description of a file system. |
| 6 | Mount target | CreateMountTarget | Creates a mount target. |
| 7 | Mount target | DeleteMountTarget | Deletes a mount target. |
| 8 | Mount target | DescribeMountTargets | Queries the information of mount targets. |
| 9 | Mount target | ModifyMountTarget | Modifies a mount target. |
| 10 | Permission group | CreateAccessGroup | Creates a permission group. |
| 11 | Permission group | DeleteAccessGroup | Deletes a permission group. |
| 12 | Permission group | DescribeAccessGroups | Queries the information of permission groups. |
| 13 | Permission group | ModifyAccessGroup | Modifies a permission group. |
| 14 | Permission group | CreateAccessRule | Creates a rule for a permission group. |
| 15 | Permission group | DeleteAccessRule | Deletes a rule from a permission group. |
| 16 | Permission group | DescribeAccessRules | Queries the information of rules. |
| 17 | Permission group | ModifyAccessRule | Modifies a rule in a permission group. |

**Common request parameters**

Common request parameters are available to all APIs. Table 1. Common request parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Format | String | No | The type of response. Valid values: JSON and XML. Default value: JSON. |   |   |
| Version | String | Yes | The API version, which is represented as a date in the format of YYYY-MM-DD . The current API version is 2017-06-26. |   |   |
| AccessKeyId | String | Yes | The AccessKey ID that is used to access services. For more information, see Obtain an AccessKey pair. |   |   |
| Signature | String | Yes | The string that represents signature. |   |   |
| SignatureMethod | String | Yes | The type of signature. Valid value: HMAC-SHA1. |   |   |
| Timestamp | String | Yes | The time when you send the request. Specify the time in the ISO 8601 standard in the YYYY-MM- DDThh:mm:ssZ format. The time must be in UTC. For example, 2017-05-26T12:00:00Z. |   |   |
|   |   |   |   | YYYY-MM- |   |
| SignatureVersion | String | Yes | The version of the signature algorithm. The current version is 1.0. |   |   |
| SecurityToken | String | No | If Security Token Service (STS) credentials are required, you must specify this parameter. |   |   |
| SignatureNonce | String | No | A unique random number. This parameter is used to prevent replay attacks. You must use different random numbers for different requests. |   |   |

|   | DDThh:mm:ssZ |
|---|---|

**Sample request**

```
GET https://nas.regionid.example.com/?Action=<Action> &Format=xml &Version=2017-06-26 &AccessKeyId=key-test &Signature=Pc5***%3D &SignatureMethod=HMAC-SHA1 &SignatureNonce=15215528852396 &SignatureVersion=1.0 &Timestamp=2012-06-01T12:00:00Z ...
```

**Endpoints**

The format of a NAS API endpoint is described in Generate the endpoint of ASAPI.

**Protocols**

You can send API requests by using HTTP or HTTPS. We recommend that you use HTTPS to ensure high security.

**Request methods**

You can send requests by using the HTTP GET method. This method requires that you specify request parameters in the request URL.

**Request parameters**

You must specify the required operation for the Action parameter of each request, such as `DescribeRegions` . Each operation must include common request parameters and other request parameters that are specific to the operation.

**Character encoding**

Requests or responses are all encoded by `UTF-8` . Queries available regions.

| PageNumber | Integer | No | 1 | The number of the page to return. Pages start from page 1. Default value: 1. |

Note An Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance can access a NAS file system in the same region but a different zone. We recommend that you select the zone where the ECS instance resides. This prevents cross-zone latency between the file system and the ECS instance. |

The description must start with a letter but cannot start with http:// or https:// . The description can contain digits, colons (:), underscores (), and hyphens (-). _ |

## 3 EBS

### 3.1 Usage notes

If you call an API operation to use a feature of Elastic Block Storage (EBS), you must specify a service name and an API version. The service name and API version vary depending on the feature that you want to use. To use an EBS feature related to cloud disks, snapshots, or storage sets, call the corresponding API operation by using an Elastic Computer Service (ECS) SDK. When you use an ECS SDK to call the corresponding API operation, specify ecs as the service name and 2014-05-26 as the API version. To use the asynchronous replication or replication pair-consistent group feature of EBS, call the corresponding API operation by using an EBS SDK. When you use an EBS SDK to call the corresponding API operation, specify ebs as the service name and 2021-07-30 as the API version.

**Important**

Asynchronous replication works based on cloud disks. Therefore, if you want to use the asynchronous replication or replication pair-consistent group feature, we recommend that you also install an ECS SDK.

### 3.2 Preparations

You can log on to the API Tool console from the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Prerequisites**

Before you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, the endpoint of the console is obtained from the deployment personnel. A browser is available. We recommend that you use Google Chrome.

**Procedure**

1. Enter the URL of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console in the address bar and press Enter.
2. Enter your username and password.
Obtain the username and password that are used to log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console from the operations administrator.

**Note**

When you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console for the first time, you must change the password of your account. For security purposes, your password must meet the minimum complexity requirements. The password must be 10 to 32 characters in length and must contain at least two of the following character types: Uppercase or lowercase letters Digits Special characters, which include ! @ # $ %
3. Click **Log On**.
4. If your account has multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled, perform corresponding operations in the following scenarios:
You log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console for the first time after MFA is enabled by the administrator. a. On the Bind Virtual MFA Device page, bind an MFA device. b. Enter the username and password again as in Step 2 and click **Log On**. c. Enter a six-digit MFA verification code and click **Authenticate**. You have enabled MFA and bound an MFA device. Enter a six-digit MFA verification code and click **Authenticate**.

**Note**

For more information, see the **Bind a virtual MFA device to enable MFA** topic in **Apsara Uni-manager Management Console User**
**Guide**.
5. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Others > API Tool**.
To call API operations by using an SDK, you must first obtain information about the service name, API operation name, and API version.

**Background information**

The information on the API Directory page of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console is for reference only. For more information about how to call API operations, see the developer guides of cloud services. If the information on the API Directory page is different from that in the developer guide of a cloud service, the information in the developer guide prevails.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Products** and choose **Others** > **API Tool**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **API Directory**.
4. On the **API Directory** page, select the required cloud service from the Product Name drop-down list, enter a keyword of an operation name in the
search box, and then click Search.
5. In the search result, you can view the **cloud service name**, **API operation name**, and **API version**.
Access credentials can be assigned by RAM or STS. You can use access credentials assigned by either of the preceding services for authentication when you call API operations. This topic describes how to obtain access credentials that are assigned by RAM.

**Background information**

An AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret are used to implement symmetric encryption and verify the identity of a request sender. The AccessKey ID is used to identify a user. The AccessKey secret is a string that is used to encrypt a signature. RAM and STS assign the following access credentials to a request sender: RAM: an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. STS: an AccessKey ID, an AccessKey secret, and a security token. For more information, see Obtain access credentials assigned by STS. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides AccessKey pairs for personal accounts and organizations. Only operations administrators and the administrators of level-1 organizations can obtain the AccessKey pairs of organizations. We recommend that you use the AccessKey pairs of personal accounts to call the API operations provided by the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and cloud services. If you use the AccessKey pair of a personal account, configure the request headers that are described in the following table for access control. Otherwise, an error that indicates insufficient permissions may occur.

**Warning**

The AccessKey pair of a personal account is managed by the permission system of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. If you need to obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, make sure that your operation is allowed by an administrator. This improves security.

| Request header | Description |
|---|---|
| x-acs-regionid | The ID of the region. Example: cn-hangzhou-*. |
| x-acs-organizationid | The ID of the organization in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For information about how to obtain an organization ID, see the GetOrganizationList section in Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Developer Guide. |
| x-acs-resourcegroupid | The ID of the resource set in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For information about how to obtain a resource set ID, see the ListResourceGroup section in Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Developer Guide. |
| x-acs-instanceid | The ID of the instance on which you want to perform the operation. For example, you can use the ID of an ECS instance obtained from the ECS instance list. |

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account**

To obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account, perform the following steps:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the upper-right corner of the homepage, click the profile picture and then click **User Information**.
3. In the **AccessKey Pair** section, view the AccessKey pair of your account.

**Note**

The AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. These credentials provide you with full permissions on Apsara Stack resources within your account. You must keep the AccessKey pair confidential.

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization**

To obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, perform the following steps:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose .
4. In the organization navigation tree, click the name of the level-1 organization whose AccessKey pair you want to obtain.
5. Click **Management AccessKey**.
6. In the Management AccessKey dialog box, view the AccessKey pair of the organization.
This topic describes how to use Security Token Service (STS) to call API operations of Elastic Block Storage (EBS).

**Background information**

Apsara Stack STS allows you to manage temporary access credentials for your Apsara Stack resources. You can use STS to call API operations in Apsara Stack. To call API operations in Apsara Stack by using STS, you must obtain an AccessKey ID, an AccessKey secret, and a security token assigned by STS.

**Procedure**

1. Obtain the Apsara Stack Resource Name (ARN) of your `Resource Access Management (RAM) role` .
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the upper-right corner of the homepage, click the profile picture and click **User Information**. iii. On the page that appears, click **View Current Role Policy**. In the **View Policies of Current Role** dialog box, view the ARN of your `RAM role` .
2. Obtain the access credential assigned by STS.

**Note**

You must replace the variables in the following code with actual values. Delete the angle brackets (<>) before you submit the code. Variables: <yourRegionID>: Replace this variable with your region ID. <yourAccessKeyID>: Replace this variable with your AccessKey ID. <yourAccessKeySecret>: Replace this variable with your AccessKey secret. <yourRoleSessionName>: Replace this variable with the name of the current session. <yourRoleArn>: Replace this variable with the ARN of your RAM role. <sts.aliyuns.com>: Replace this variable with the STS endpoint.

```java
public static void main(String[] args) {
    // Create a DefaultAcsClient instance and initialize the instance.
    // Replace <yourRegionID>, <yourAccessKeyID>, and <yourAccessKeySecret> with your region ID, AccessKey ID, and AccessKey secret.
    DefaultProfile profile = DefaultProfile.getProfile("<yourRegionID>", "<yourAccessKeyID>", "<yourAccessKeySecret>");
    HttpClientConfig clientConfig = HttpClientConfig.getDefault();
    clientConfig.setIgnoreSSLCerts(true);
    clientConfig.setProtocolType(ProtocolType.HTTPS);
    profile.setHttpClientConfig(clientConfig);
    IAcsClient client = new DefaultAcsClient(profile);
    String assumeRole = callAssumeRole(client);
    if (StringUtils.isEmpty(assumeRole)) return;
    JSONObject assumeRoleJson = JSONObject.parseObject(assumeRole);
    JSONObject credentials = assumeRoleJson.getJSONObject("Credentials");
    // Obtain the access credentials assigned by STS.
    String stsAK = credentials.getString("AccessKeyId");
    String stsSK = credentials.getString("AccessKeySecret");
    String stsToken = credentials.getString("SecurityToken");
private static String callAssumeRole(IAcsClient client) {
    CommonRequest request = new CommonRequest();
    // Replace sts.aliyuns.com with the actual endpoint of STS. The endpoint of STS is in the sts-vpc.${global:region}.${global:internet-dom
ain} format.
    request.setSysDomain("sts.aliyuns.com");
    request.setSysProduct("Sts");
    request.setSysAction("AssumeRole");
    request.setSysVersion("2015-04-01");
    request.setSysMethod(MethodType.POST);
    request.setHttpContentType(FormatType.FORM);
    // Replace <yourRoleSessionName> with the name of the current session.
    request.putQueryParameter("RoleSessionName", "<yourRoleSessionName>");
    // Replace <yourRoleArn> with the ARN of the RAM role that you obtained in the preceding step.
    request.putQueryParameter("RoleArn", "<yourRoleArn>");
    try {
        CommonResponse response = client.getCommonResponse(request);
        return response.getData();
    } catch (ServerException e) {
        System.out.println(e.getErrCode());
        System.out.println(e.getErrMsg());
    } catch (ClientException e) {
        System.out.println(e.getErrCode());
        System.out.println(e.getErrMsg());
    return null;
```

3. Use the access credentials assigned by STS to call an operation of a service.

**Note**

You must replace the variables in the following code with actual values. Delete the angle brackets (<>) before you submit the code. The API version and service name that you must specify in the code vary depending on the EBS feature that you want to use. If you want to use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, you must specify **2014-05-26** as the API version and **Ecs** as the service name. If you want to use the async replication or replication pair-consistent group feature, you must specify **2021-07-30** as the API version and **ebs** as the service name. The following sample code provides an example on how to call the DescribeDisks operation to query the information about cloud disks:

```java
public static void main(String[] args) {
    // Replace <yourRegionID> with the actual region ID.
    // Replace <yourStsAccessKeyID> and <yourStsAccessKeySecret> with the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret assigned by STS.
    DefaultProfile profile = DefaultProfile.getProfile("<yourRegionID>", "<yourStsAccesskey>", "<yourStsAccessSecret>");
    HttpClientConfig clientConfig = HttpClientConfig.getDefault();
    clientConfig.setIgnoreSSLCerts(true);
    clientConfig.setProtocolType(ProtocolType.HTTPS);
    profile.setHttpClientConfig(clientConfig);
    IAcsClient client = new DefaultAcsClient(profile);
    CommonRequest request = new CommonRequest();
    request.setSysDomain("ecs.aliyuns.com");
    // Specify Ecs as the service name.
    request.setSysProduct("Ecs");
    // Specify the name of the API operation. It must be the same as the name of the API operation in API references.
    request.setSysAction("DescribeDisks");
    // Specify 2014-05-26 as the API version.
    request.setSysVersion("2014-05-26");
    request.setSysMethod(MethodType.POST);
    request.setHttpContentType(FormatType.FORM);
    // Replace <yourRegionID> with the actual region ID.
    request.putHeadParameter("x-acs-regionid", "<yourRegionID>");
    // Replace <yourStsToken> with the security token assigned by STS.
    request.putQueryParameter("SecurityToken", "<yourStsToken>");
    // Optional. Replace <yourResourceGroupID> with the actual resource set ID.
    // request.putHeadParameter("x-acs-resourcegroupid", "<yourResourceGroupID>");
    // Required. Replace <yourOrganizationID> with the actual organization ID.
    request.putHeadParameter("x-acs-organizationid", "<yourOrganizationID>");
    try {
        CommonResponse response = client.getCommonResponse(request);
        System.out.println(response.getData());
    } catch (ServerException e) {
        System.out.println(e.getErrCode());
        System.out.println(e.getErrMsg());
    } catch (ClientException e) {
        System.out.println(e.getErrCode());
        System.out.println(e.getErrMsg());
```

You must set request headers when you call API operations in Apsara Stack. This topic describes the request headers and how to obtain the values of the request headers. This topic also describes the response parameters of specific headers after you call API operations in Apsara Stack.

**Request headers**

| Request header | Description |
|---|---|
| x-acs-regionid | The ID of the region. For more information about how to obtain a region ID, see Obtain a region ID. |
| x-acs-organizationid | The ID of the organization in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For more information about how to obtain an organization ID, see Obtain an organization ID. |
| x-acs-resourcegroupid | The ID of the resource set in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For more information about how to obtain a resource set ID, see Obtain a resource set ID. |
| x-acs-instanceid | The ID of the instance on which you want to perform the operation. For more information about how to obtain an instance ID, see Obtain an instance ID. |

**Obtain a region ID**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Resources** > **Regions**.
4. In the organization navigation tree, click the name of the organization whose region ID you want to obtain.
5. Obtain the region ID in the **Regions** section on the right.

**Obtain an organization ID**

You can call the GetOrganizationList operation to obtain the organization ID. For more information, see the GetOrganizationList section in Apsara Unimanager Management Console Developer Guide.

**Obtain a resource set ID**

You can call the ListResourceGroup operation to obtain the resource set ID. For more information, see the ListResourceGroup section in Apsara Unimanager Management Console Developer Guide.

**Obtain an instance ID**

You can obtain the ID of an instance on related pages of the corresponding cloud service in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. The steps vary depending on the feature that you want to use. To use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, perform the following steps:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Elastic Compute Service**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Disks**, **Snapshots**, or **Automatic Snapshot Policies**.
4. On the page that appears, obtain a resource ID, such as a cloud disk or snapshot ID.
To use the asynchronous replication or replication pair-consistent group feature, perform the following steps:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Elastic Block Storage**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **EBS Async Replication** or **Replication Pair-Consistent Group**.
4. On the page that appears, obtain a resource ID, such as a replication pair or replication pair-consistent group ID.

**Response parameters**

The following table describes the response parameters that are returned by default when you call operations to query the instances of cloud services.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| ResourceGroupName | The name of the resource set. |
| ResourceGroup | The ID of the resource set. |
| DepartmentName | The name of the organization. |
| Department | The ID of the organization. |

This topic describes how to obtain the endpoints of ECS and EBS.

**Background information**

If you want to call API operations in Apsara Stack by using the POP gateway, you must specify the endpoint of the corresponding cloud service. You can obtain an endpoint from onsite Apsara Stack O&M engineers. You can also perform the following operations to obtain an endpoint. The endpoint that you need to obtain varies depending on the EBS feature that you want to use. If you want to use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, obtain the endpoint of ECS. For more information, see Obtain the endpoint of ECS. If you want to use the asynchronous replication or replication pair-consistent group feature, obtain the endpoint of EBS. For more information, see Obtain the endpoint of EBS.

**Obtain the endpoint of ECS**

1. Log on to the Apsara Infrastructure Management console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Apsara Infrastructure Management Framework**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Reports**.
3. On the **All Reports** page, search for `Registration Vars of Services` . In the report list that appears, click the name of the report.
4. On the **Registration Vars of Services** page, click the
icon next to **Service** and search for `ECS` .
5. Find the `ecs-yaochi` service, right-click the value in the **Service Registration** column, and then select **Show More**.
In the **Details** dialog box, view the value of **ecs-internal.openapi.endpoint**. The value indicates the `endpoint` of ECS.

**Obtain the endpoint of EBS**

1. Log on to the Apsara Infrastructure Management console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Apsara Infrastructure Management Framework**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Reports**.
3. On the **All Reports** page, search for `Registration Vars of Services` . In the report list that appears, click the name of the report.
4. On the **Registration Vars of Services** page, click the
icon next to **Service** and search for `EBS` .
5. Find the EbsTiangangApi service, right-click the value in the **Service Registration** column, and then select **Show More**.
In the **Details** dialog box, view the value of **ebstiangang.openapi.endpoint**. The value indicates the `endpoint` of EBS. If you want to call API operations in Apsara Stack by using the POP gateway, you must obtain an ECS or EBS SDK. This topic describes how to obtain an SDK. The SDK that you need to obtain varies depending on the EBS feature that you want to use. We recommend that you obtain both an ECS SDK and an EBS SDK. If you want to use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, obtain an ECS SDK. An ECS SDK encapsulates the API released on May 26, 2014. The SDK identifies callers based on their AccessKey pairs and provides features such as automatic signing to allow you to create and manage resources by calling API operations. To use the corresponding features, you must install both an ECS SDK and the Alibaba Cloud core library. For example, to use ECS SDK for Java, you must download aliyun-java-sdk-core and aliyun-java-sdk-ecs. If you want to use the asynchronous replication or replication pair-consistent group feature, obtain an EBS SDK. An EBS SDK encapsulates the API released on July 30, 2021. The SDK identifies callers based on their AccessKey pairs and provides features such as automatic signing to allow you to create and manage resources by calling API operations. To use the corresponding features, you must install both an EBS SDK and the Alibaba Cloud core library. For example, to use EBS SDK for Java, you must download aliyun-java-sdk-core and aliyun-java-sdk-ebs. An SDK includes code and examples. You can create cloud applications by using an SDK for the programming language that you require. The SDKs for Java, Python, and Go are provided. You can select an SDK from Alibaba Cloud SDKs based on your business requirements.

**Note**

We recommend that you use an SDK for Java, Python, or Go. If you use SDKs for other programming languages, the SDKs may be incompatible with your system. We recommend that you use the SDK core library that is provided on the Alibaba Cloud official website. The SDK core library is ideal for all cloud services and is compatible with Apsara Stack.

### 3.3 Java SDK call example

This topic describes how to obtain and use ECS SDK for Java and EBS SDK for Java to call API operations.

**Environment requirements**

An Apsara Stack tenant account that has the required permissions and an AccessKey pair that consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret are obtained. For more information, see Obtain access credentials assigned by RAM. The endpoint of the corresponding service is obtained. The service varies depending on the feature that you want to use. For more information, see Obtain an endpoint. Java Development Kit (JDK) 1.8 or later is installed. If you use Apache Maven to manage a Java project, you need to only import the JAR file to the pom.xml file of the project. To use an SDK of a service, you must install both the SDK core library and the SDK. We recommend that you use V4.5.17 or later of the core library. In this example, ECS SDK for Java V4.23.2 and EBS SDK for Java V1.0.3 are used. For more information, see Install ECS or EBS SDK for Java.

**Use ECS or EBS SDK for Java**

To use ECS or EBS SDK for Java, perform the following steps:
1. Create a DefaultAcsClient instance and initialize the instance.
2. Create an API request and set the required parameters.
3. Send the API request and handle the response or exceptions.
The API version and service name that you must specify in the code vary depending on the EBS feature that you want to use. If you want to use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, you must specify **2014-05-26** as the API version and **Ecs** as the service name. If you want to use the asynchronous replication or replication pair-consistent group feature, you must specify **2021-07-30** as the API version and
**ebs** as the service name.
The following sample code provides an example in which the DescribeDisks operation is called to query the information about cloud disks:

**Note**

You must replace the variables in the following code with actual values. Delete the angle brackets (<>) before you submit the code. Variables: <yourRegionID>: Replace the variable with the actual region ID. <yourAccessKeyID>: Replace the variable with your AccessKey ID. <yourAccessKeySecret>: Replace the variable with your AccessKey secret. <Product>: Replace the variable with the name of the required service. <Endpoint>: Replace the variable with the endpoint of the required service. <readTimeout>: Replace the variable with a read timeout period based on your business requirements. Unit: milliseconds. <connectionTimeout>: Replace the variable with a connection timeout period based on your business requirements. Unit: milliseconds. <maxRequestsPerHost>: Replace the variable with the maximum number of requests that are supported by each host. <maxRequests>: Replace the variable with the maximum number of requests. <http://192.168.XX:33XX>: Replace the variable with the IP address and port of the proxy that you use.

```java
       clientConfig.setProtocolType(ProtocolType.HTTP); // Optional. The request protocol. Default value: HTTP.

       clientConfig.setHttpProxy("<http://192.168.XX:33XX>");
```

This topic describes how to install and use ECS SDK for Java and EBS SDK for Java. ECS or EBS SDK for Java supports JDK 1.8 or later. You can install ECS or EBS SDK for Java by adding Maven dependencies or downloading the SDK package. For more information, see Alibaba Cloud SDKs. To use EBS features, you must install both the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Java and ECS or EBS SDK for Java. We recommend that you use V4.5.17 or later of the core library. In this example, ECS SDK for Java V4.23.2 and EBS SDK for Java V1.0.3 are used. The SDK that you need to install varies depending on the EBS feature that you want to use. We recommend that you install both ECS SDK for Java and EBS SDK for Java. To use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, you must install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Java and ECS SDK for Java. In addition, you must add the following dependencies to the pom.xml file. For more information about the SDK version, see Alibaba Cloud SDKs.

```xml
<!-- Alibaba Cloud SDK for Java --> <dependency>
    <groupId>com.aliyun</groupId>
    <artifactId>aliyun-java-sdk-core</artifactId>
    <version>4.5.17</version>
</dependency> <!-- ECS Java SDK --> <dependency>
    <groupId>com.aliyun</groupId>
    <artifactId>aliyun-java-sdk-ecs</artifactId>
    <version>4.23.2</version>
</dependency>
```

To use the asynchronous replication or replication pair-consistent group feature, you must install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Java and EBS SDK for Java. In addition, you must add the following dependencies to the pom.xml file. For more information about the SDK version, see Alibaba Cloud SDKs.

```xml
<!-- Alibaba Cloud SDK for Java --> <dependency>
    <groupId>com.aliyun</groupId>
    <artifactId>aliyun-java-sdk-core</artifactId>
    <version>4.5.17</version>
</dependency> <!-- EBS Java SDK--> <dependency>
```

This topic describes how to use ECS SDK for Java and EBS SDK for Java to initiate requests.

**Use ECS SDK for Java to initiate a request**

1. Create an AcsClient instance.

```
IAcsClient client = new DefaultAcsClient(profile);
```

2. Create a request.
The naming convention for requests is ${apiName}Request . ${apiName} indicates the API operation name. Example: `DescribeDisksRequest` . When the SDKs of multiple services are used, different requests may have the same name. Differentiate the requests by SDK.

```
DescribeDisksRequest(); // Set service-related parameters. request.setPageSize(10); request.setPageNumber(1); // Specify the organization ID and resource set ID. This way, resources can be isolated. Modify the values of the headers based on your busi ness requirements. request.putHeaderParameter("x-acs-organizationid", "1"); request.putHeaderParameter("x-acs-resourcegroupid", "");
```

3. Initiate the request and handle the response.

| DescribeDisksResponse response; try { response = client.getAcsResponse(request); System.out.println(response.getRequestId()); System.out.println(response.getTotalCount()); } catch (ServerException e) { e.printStackTrace(); } catch (ClientException e) { e.printStackTrace(); } |   |   |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|

**Use EBS SDK for Java to initiate a request**

1. Create a client instance.

```
public static com.aliyun.ebs20210730.Client createClient(String accessKeyId, String accessKeySecret) throws Exception {

        return new com.aliyun.ebs20210730.Client(config);
```

```java
DescribeDiskReplicaPairsResponse resp = client.describeDiskReplicaPairs(describeDiskReplicaPairsRequest); for (int i = 0; i < resp.body.getReplicaPairs().size(); i++) {
```

If the server or SDK encounters an error when you use SDK for Java, it returns an error response. The error response contains an error code and an error message. In most cases, you do not need to handle the errors returned by SDK for Java. You need to only handle the errors returned by the server based on error messages. `ServerException` indicates a server error. `ClientException` indicates an SDK error. For example, when the following error occurs, you can modify the AccessKey ID based on the error message to solve the problem:

```
com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ClientException: InvalidAccessKeyId.NotFound : Specified access key is not found.
```

If you want to handle SDK errors, refer to the following example to write your code:

```java
try {
    FooResponse response = client.getAcsResponse(request);
    // Handle the response.
    // ...
}catch (ServerException e){
    // You can add your logic to handle errors.
    // For example, print the error message.
    System.out.println("ErrorCode=" + e.getErrCode());
    System.out.println("ErrorMessage=" + e.getErrMsg());
    // If the error persists, you can submit a ticket with the request ID included.
    System.out.println("ResponseId=" + e.getRequestId());
}catch (ClientException e){
    // You can add your logic to handle errors.
    // For example, print the error message.
    System.out.println("ErrorCode=" + e.getErrCode());
    System.out.println("ErrorMessage=" + e.getErrMsg());
```

If you want to call an ECS or EBS API operation without an SDK, or the request and response of the API operation that you call by using an SDK cannot meet your business requirements, you can use CommonRequest to call the API operation. You can use CommonRequest to call all API operations.

**Benefits**

CommonRequest provides the following benefits: Lightweight: You need to only download the core package. You do not need to download and install the SDKs of services. Easy to use: You can call the newly released API operations of a service without the need to update the SDK of the service. Fast iteration.

**Use CommonRequest to call an API operation**

If you want to send a CommonRequest request, you must obtain the values of the following parameters. You can obtain the values of these parameters from the related topics about ECS API operations. Domain: the endpoint of the service. Version: the version number of the API. Specify the version number in the YYYY-MM-DD format. You can obtain the API version from the sections about common parameters in the related topics about API operations. Action: the name of the API operation that you want to call.

| You must obtain the value of the Action para For example, if you want to use CommonRequest |   | Action |   | para |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|   | CommonRequest |   |   |   |
| request.setSysAction("RunInstances") |   |   | format. |   |

You must obtain the value of the `Action` parameter and specify the API operation in the `request.setSysAction("<Action>")` format. For example, if you want to use `CommonRequest` to call the `RunInstances` operation, you must specify the API operation in the

### 3.4 Python SDK call example

This topic describes how to obtain and use ECS SDK for Python and EBS SDK for Python to call API operations. An Apsara Stack tenant account that has the required permissions and an AccessKey pair are obtained. An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. For more information, see Obtain access credentials assigned by RAM. The endpoint of the corresponding service is obtained. The service varies based on the feature that you want to use. For more information, see Obtain an endpoint.

**Install SDKs for Python**

To use EBS features, you must install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python and the SDK for Python of the required cloud service. The SDK that you must install varies based on the EBS feature that you want to use. We recommend that you install ECS SDK for Python and EBS SDK for Python. To use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, you must install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python and ECS SDK for Python. To use the asynchronous replication feature or the replication pair-consistent group feature, you must install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python and EBS SDK for Python. To install the required SDKs for Python, perform the following steps:
1. Install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python.
If you use Python 2.x, run the following command:

```
pip install aliyun-python-sdk-core
```

If you use Python 3.x, run the following command:

```
pip3 install aliyun-python-sdk-core-v3
```

2. Install the SDK for Python of the required cloud service based on your business requirements.
Install ECS SDK for Python. If you use Python 2.x, run the following command:

```
pip install aliyun-python-sdk-ecs
```

If you use Python 3.x, run the following command:

```
pip3 install aliyun-python-sdk-ecs
```

Install EBS SDK for Python. If you use Python 2.x, run the following command:

```
pip install alibabacloud_ebs20210730==1.0.3
```

If you use Python 3.x, run the following command:

```
pip3 install alibabacloud_ebs20210730==1.0.3
```

**Use SDKs for Python**

To use the required SDKs for Python, perform the following steps:
1. Create a client. When you create a client, you must obtain a region ID, AccessKey ID, and AccessKey secret.
2. Create an API request and configure the required parameters.
3. Send the API request, and check the response or handle exceptions.
The API version and service name that you must specify in the code vary based on the EBS feature that you want to use. If you want to use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, you must specify **2014-05-26** as the API version and **Ecs** as the service name. If you want to use the asynchronous replication feature or the replication pair-consistent group feature, you must specify **2021-07-30** as the API version and **ebs** as the service name.

**Note**

In the following sample code, replace the variables with actual values. Delete the angle brackets (<>) from the code. Variables: <yourRegionID>: Replace this variable with your region ID. <yourAccessKeyID>: Replace this variable with your AccessKey ID. <yourAccessKeySecret>: Replace this variable with your AccessKey secret. <ecs.aliyuns.com>: Replace this variable with the endpoint of the service. <http://192.168.XX:33XX>: Replace this variable with the IP address and port of the proxy that you use. The following sample code provides an example on how to call the DescribeDisks operation to query the information about cloud disks:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python
#coding=utf-8
from aliyunsdkcore import client from aliyunsdkcore.profile import region_provider from aliyunsdkecs.request.v20140526 import DescribeDisksRequest
# global config
region_id = '<yourRegionID>' # Specify your region ID. access_key = '<yourAccessKeyID>' # Specify your AccessKey ID. access_secret = '<yourAccessKeySecret>' # Specify your AccessKey secret. http_proxy='<http://192.168.XX:33XX>', # Specify the IP address and port of the HTTP proxy.
# product config
product_name = 'ECS' # Specify the name of the required service. endpoint = '<ecs.aliyuns.com>' # Specify the endpoint of the required service.
# create client
region_provider.modify_point(product_name, region_id, endpoint) clt = client.AcsClient(access_key, access_secret, region_id)
# setup request
request = DescribeDisksRequest.DescribeDisksRequest() request.set_accept_format('json') # Specify the response format.
# get response
response = clt.do_action_with_exception(request) print(response)
```

This topic describes how to install and use ECS SDK for Python and EBS SDK for Python.

**Background information**

Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python supports Python 2.6.x, Python 2.7.x, Python 3.x, and later versions. You can install Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python by using pip.

**Note**

To use Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python to access an Apsara Stack service, you must install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python. For example, if you want to use ECS SDK for Python, you must install both the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python and ECS SDK for Python. To use EBS features, you must install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python and the SDK for Python of the required cloud service. The SDK that you must install varies based on the EBS feature that you want to use. We recommend that you install ECS SDK for Python and EBS SDK for Python. To use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, you must install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python and ECS SDK for Python. To use the asynchronous replication feature or the replication pair-consistent group feature, you must install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python and EBS SDK for Python. To install ECS or EBS SDK for Python, perform the following steps:
1. Install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python.
If you use Python 2.x, run the following command:

```
pip install aliyun-python-sdk-core
```

If you use Python 3.x, run the following command:

```
pip3 install aliyun-python-sdk-core-v3
```

2. Install the SDK for Python of the required cloud service based on your business requirements.
Install ECS SDK for Python. If you use Python 2.x, run the following command:

```
pip install aliyun-python-sdk-ecs
```

If you use Python 3.x, run the following command:

```
pip3 install aliyun-python-sdk-ecs
```

Install EBS SDK for Python. If you use Python 2.x, run the following command:

```
pip install alibabacloud_ebs20210730==1.0.3
```

If you use Python 3.x, run the following command:

```
pip3 install alibabacloud_ebs20210730==1.0.3
```

When you use Alibaba Cloud SDKs to access Apsara Stack services, you must provide an Apsara Stack tenant account for authentication. This topic describes how to configure authentication credentials. Alibaba Cloud SDK for Python allows you to complete the authentication process by using an AccessKey pair. For more information about how to obtain an AccessKey pair, see Obtain access credentials assigned by RAM. If you want to use your AccessKey pair to access Apsara Stack, you must configure the AccessKey pair as credentials when you initialize a client instance.

**Note**

Do not disclose any code that contains your AccessKey pair. For example, do not commit the code to public GitHub projects. Otherwise, your account may be compromised.

```python
from aliyunsdkcore import client clt = client.AcsClient(access_key, acces_secret, region_id)
```

Apsara Stack SDK for Python allows you to initiate API requests over HTTP and HTTPS. You can specify the HTTP or HTTPS protocol for a specific request, or set a global default protocol.

**Note**

The default HTTP or HTTPS protocol of a service takes precedence over the global default protocol.

**Add OpenSSL support**

The HTTPS protocol support of Apsara Stack SDK for Python is based on the OpenSSL support in Python. To use Apsara Stack SDK for Python to send HTTPS requests, you must add OpenSSL support in Python. OpenSSL supports TLS 1.2 and later.

| Run the | python -c "import ssl" | c |
|---|---|---|
| ImportError: No module named ssl |   |   |

Run the `python -c "import ssl"` command to check whether your Python environment supports OpenSSL. If the error message `ImportError: No module named ssl` is not returned, OpenSSL is already supported. Otherwise, run the following command to install it:

```
pip install pyopenssl
```

**Set the protocol to HTTP or HTTPS for a single request**

The following sample code provides an example on how to set HTTPS as the protocol for a request:

```bash
request = DescribeInstancesRequest() request.set_protocol_type("https")
# Set the value to https or http.
```

**Set a global default protocol**

The following sample code provides an example on how to set a global default protocol:


If an error occurs on the server side or SDK side when you use the Python SDK, the Python SDK returns the corresponding exception message. An exception message contains the detailed error information, namely the error code and the error message. Generally, you are not required to handle the errors returned by the Python SDK. You are only required to handle the errors on the server side according to the error message. `ServerException` is the error message on the server side. `ClientException` is the error message on the SDK side. For example, if the following error occurs, modify the ID of AccessKey according to the detailed error message.

```
aliyunsdkcore.acs\_exception.exceptions.ServerException: HTTP Status: 404 Error:InvalidAccessKeyId.NotFound Specified access key is not found.
```

To handle the errors returned by the Python SDK, see the following code example for reference:

```bash
try:
    response = client.do_action_with_exception(request)
except ServerException as e:
    # Add your own error handling logic here.
    # For example, print the detailed error message.
    print e.get_http_status()
    print e.get_error_code()
    print e.get_error_msg()
```

If you want to call an ECS or EBS API operation without an SDK, or the request and response of the API operation that you call by using an SDK cannot meet your business requirements, you can use CommonRequest to call the API operation. You can use CommonRequest to call all API operations.

**Benefits**

CommonRequest provides the following benefits: Lightweight: You only need to download the core package. You do not need to download and install SDKs of Apsara Stack services. Easy to use: You can call the newly released API operations of a service without the need to update the SDK of the service. Fast in iteration.

**Use CommonRequest to call an API operation**

If you want to send a CommonRequest request, you must obtain the values of the following parameters. You can obtain the values of these parameters from the related topics about API operations. Domain: the endpoint of the service. Version: the version number of the API. Specify the version number in the YYYY-MM-DD format. You can obtain the API version from the sections about common parameters in the related topics about API operations. Action: the name of the API operation that you want to call.

| You must obtain the value of the Action para For example, if you want to use CommonRequest |   | Action | para |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|   | CommonRequest |   |   |   |
| request.set_action_name('RunInstances') |   |   |   | form |

You must obtain the value of the `Action` parameter and specify the API operation in the `request.set_action_name('Action')` format. For example, if you want to use `CommonRequest` to call the `RunInstances` operation, you must specify the API operation in the

**Example: Call an RPC API operation**

The API version and service name that you must specify in the code vary depending on the EBS feature that you want to use. If you want to use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, you must specify **2014-05-26** as the API version and **Ecs** as the service name. If you want to use the asynchronous replication or replication pair-consistent group feature, you must specify **2021-07-30** as the API version and **ebs** as the service name. The following sample code provides an example in which the DescribeDisks operation is called to query the information about cloud disks:

**Note**

You must replace the variables in the following code with actual values. Delete the angle brackets (<>) before you submit the code. Variables: <yourRegionID>: Replace the variable with the actual region ID. <yourAccessKeyID>: Replace the variable with your AccessKey ID. <yourAccessKeySecret>: Replace the variable with your AccessKey secret. <yourSecurityToken>: Replace the variable with your security token. <yourResourceGroupID>: Replace the variable with the resource set ID. <yourOrganizationID>: Replace the variable with the organization ID. <yourInstanceID>: Replace the variable with the instance ID. <ecs.aliyuncs.com>: Replace the variable with the endpoint of the required service.

```xml
#!/usr/bin/env python
# coding=utf-8
from aliyunsdkcore.client import AcsClient from aliyunsdkcore.request import CommonRequest
# Specify the AccessKey ID, AccessKey secret, and region ID.
client = AcsClient('{<yourAccessKeyID>}', '{<yourAccessKeySecret>}', '{<yourRegionID>}') request = CommonRequest() request.set_product('Ecs') request.set_action_name('DescribeDisks') request.set_version('2014-05-26') request.set_domain('<ecs.aliyuncs.com>') # Specify the endpoint of the required service.
# or:
# request = = CommonRequest(product='Ecs', action_name='DescribeInstanceStatus',version='2014-05-26',domain='ecs.aliyuncs.com')
######
# Specify the request protocol. Valid values: https and http. Default value: http.
# The following example shows how to set the request protocol to HTTPS:
# request.set_protocol_type('https')
######
request.set_accept_format('json') request.set_method('POST') request.add_query_param('PageNumber', '1') request.add_query_param('PageSize', '30')
######
# If you use the access credentials assigned by STS to call an RPC API operation, you must specify the SecurityToken parameter in the request.
# Format:
# request.add_query_param("SecurityToken", "<yourSecurityToken>");
# Specify your security token.
######
# Optional. Specify the resource set ID.
request.add_header("x-acs-resourcegroupid", "<yourResourceGroupID>")
# Required. Specify the organization ID.
request.add_header("x-acs-organizationid", "<yourOrganizationID>")
# Required. Specify the source of the API call.
request.add_header("x-acs-caller-sdk-source","ApiTestDemo")
# Optional. Specify the region ID. If you use Apsara Stack Enterprise V3.15.0 or earlier, you must replace <yourRegionID> with the actual regi
on ID. request.add_header("x-acs-regionid", "<yourRegionID>")
# Optional. Specify the instance ID. If you want to modify, delete, or view the details of a specific instance, you must replace
<yourInstanceID> with the actual instance ID.
# request.add_header("x-acs-instanceid", "<yourInstanceID>")
response = client.do_action_with_exception(request)
# python2:  print(response)
print(str(response, encoding = 'utf-8'))
```

### 3.5 Go SDK call example

Alibaba Cloud SDK for Go allows you to access services without complex coding. This topic describes how to download and use ECS SDK for Go and EBS SDK for Go.

**Make preparations**

Obtain an authorized account and an AccessKey pair, consisting of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. For more information, see Obtain access credentials assigned by RAM. Obtain the endpoint of the service that is involved based on the feature that you want to use. For more information, see Obtain an endpoint.

**Install the core package of Alibaba Cloud SDK for Go**

Alibaba Cloud SDK for Go supports Go 1.10.x and later. You can run the following command to install the core package:

```
go get -u github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk
```

**Use the SDKs for Go**

To use an SDK for Go, perform the following steps:
1. Initialize a client instance.
2. Create an API request and set the required parameters.
3. Initiate the API request and process the response or exception.
The API version and service name that you must specify in the code vary depending on the EBS feature that you want to use. If you want to use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, you must specify **2014-05-26** as the API version and **Ecs** as the service name. If you want to use the asynchronous replication or replication pair-consistent group feature, you must specify **2021-07-30** as the API version and
**ebs** as the service name.

**Note**

You must replace the variables in the following code with actual values. Delete the angle brackets (<>) before you submit the code. Variables: <yourRegionID>: Replace the variable with the actual region ID. <yourAccessKeyID>: Replace the variable with your AccessKey ID. <yourAccessKeySecret>: Replace the variable with your AccessKey secret. <Endpoint>: Replace the variable with the endpoint of the required service. <http://192.168.XX:33XX>: Replace the variable with the IP address and port of the proxy that you use. The following sample code provides an example in which the DescribeDisks operation is called to query the information about cloud disks:

```java
package main import (
    "github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/services/ecs"
    "github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/requests"
    "fmt"
```

`)`

```
func main() {
    // Create an ecsClient instance.
    ecsClient, err := ecs.NewClientWithAccessKey(
        "<yourRegionID>",             // Replace the variable with the actual region ID.
        "<yourAccessKeyID>",         // Replace the variable with your AccessKey ID.
        "<yourAccessKeySecret>")        // Replace the variable with your AccessKey secret.
    if err != nil {
        // Handle exceptions.
        panic(err)
    // Configure the proxy.
    ecsClient.SetHttpProxy("https://192.168.XX:33XX>")   // Configure the HTTP proxy.
    ecsClient.GetHttpProxy()                          // Query the HTTP proxy.
    ecsClient.SetHttpsProxy("<https://192.168.XX:33XX>")   // Configure the HTTPS proxy.
    ecsClient.GetHttpsProxy()                           // Query the HTTPS proxy.
    ecsClient.SetNoProxy("127.0.0.1,localhost")     // Configure the IP addresses or domain names that do not require proxies.
    ecsClient.GetNoProxy()                          // Query the IP addresses or domain names that do not require proxies.
    // Create an API request and set the parameters.
    request := ecs.DescribeDisksRequest()
    // Specify the endpoint of the service.
    request.Domain = "<Endpoint>"
    // Set request.PageSize to 10.
    request.PageSize = requests.NewInteger(10)
    // Initiate the request and handle exceptions.
    response, err := ecsClient.DescribeInstances(request)
    if err != nil {
        // Handle exceptions.
        panic(err)
    fmt.Println(response)
```

When you use Alibaba Cloud SDK for Go, errors may occur. If an error occurs on the server or in the SDK, a `ServerError` or a `ClientError` is returned. Both error types are included in `sdk.errors` . The errors conform to the standard Go error interface and can be handled in a similar way as standard Go errors. You can use the following code to troubleshoot an error:

```
response,err := ecsClient.DescribeDisks(request) if err != nil {
    // Obtain the error information.
   err.Error()
```

**ClientError**

If an error occurs in the SDK when you send a request and the error cannot be automatically handled, the SDK returns a `ClientError` .

| The following sample code shows how to determine and obtain the error message in a | ClientError | returned by ECS SDK for Go: |
|---|---|---|
| Note If you use a specific error struct, you must add the error package github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/errors by using the following code: package main import ( "github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/services/ecs" // Replace ecs with the name of the service. "github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/requests" // The error package that you want to add. "github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/errors" "fmt" ) |   |   |

```
response, err := ecsClient.DescribeDisks(request) if clientError, ok := err.(*errors.ClientError); ok{
    // Obtain the error code.
    clientError.ErrorCode()
    // Obtain the error message.
    clientError.Message()
    // Obtain the original error. The return value may be nil.
    clientError.OriginError()
```

**ServerError**

If the server returns an error response, the SDK wraps the response into a `ServerError` and returns it to the client. In this case, you can still obtain the original HTTP response from Response.

| The following sample code shows how to determine and obtain the error message in a | ServerError | and | Response | returned by ECS SDK for Go: |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Note If you use a specific error struct, you must add the error package github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/errors by using the following code: import ( "github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/services/ecs" // Replace ecs with the name of the service. "github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/requests" // The error package that you want to add. "github.com/aliyun/alibaba-cloud-sdk-go/sdk/errors" "fmt" ) |   |   |   |   |

```
response, err := ecsClient.DescribeDisks(request) if serverError, ok := err.(*errors.ServerError); ok{
    // Obtain the error code.
    serverError.ErrorCode()
    // Obtain the error message.
    serverError.Message()
    // Obtain the original HTTP response.
    response.GetOriginHttpResponse()
```

### 3.6 API references

To call an EBS API operation, you can send an HTTP GET request to the endpoint of the EBS server. You must set the relevant request parameters in the request based on the operation description. Then, the system returns the processing result of the request. All requests and responses are UTF-8 encoded.

**Endpoint**

For information about how to obtain the endpoints of services, see Obtain an endpoint.

**Request method**

You can call EBS API operations by sending HTTP GET requests. If you use this method, you must include request parameters in request URLs.

**Protocols**

You can send API requests over HTTP or HTTPS. We recommend that you use HTTPS to ensure higher security.

**Request parameters**

In each request, you must set the Action parameter to specify the operation that you want to perform. For example, you can set the Action parameter to CreateDisk. You must also specify the common request parameters and operation-specific parameters.

**Encoding format**

Requests and responses are encoded in UTF-8. To ensure the security of your account, we recommend that you use a RAM user to call API operations. Before you call an EBS API operation as a RAM user, you must grant the RAM user the required permissions by creating a policy and attaching the policy to the RAM user. In RAM, you can authorize a RAM user to call the following API operations on EBS resources:

| Category | Operation |
|---|---|

| Cloud disk | CreateDisk DescribeDisks AttachDisk DetachDisk ModifyDiskAttribute ReInitDisk ResetDisk DeleteDisk |
|---|---|
| Snapshot | CreateSnapshot DeleteSnapshot DescribeSnapshots CopySnapshot DescribeSnapshotLinks DescribeSnapshotsUsage CreateAutoSnapshotPolicy DeleteAutoSnapshotPolicy ModifyAutoSnapshotPolicyEx ModifySnapshotAttribute DescribeAutoSnapshotPolicyEX ApplyAutoSnapshotPolicy CancelAutoSnapshotPolicy CreateSnapshotGroup DescribeSnapshotGroups DeleteSnapshotGroup ModifySnapshotGroup |
| Asynchronous replication | CreateDiskReplicaPair StartDiskReplicaPair DescribeDiskReplicaPairs DescribeDiskReplicaPairProgress ModifyDiskReplicaPair FailoverDiskReplicaPair ReprotectDiskReplicaPair StopDiskReplicaPair DeleteDiskReplicaPair |
| Replication pair-consistent group | CreateDiskReplicaGroup AddDiskReplicaPair StartDiskReplicaGroup DescribeDiskReplicaGroups ModifyDiskReplicaGroup FailoverDiskReplicaGroup ReprotectDiskReplicaGroup RemoveDiskReplicaPair StopDiskReplicaGroup DeleteDiskReplicaGroup |

EBS verifies the identity of the sender of each access request. Therefore, all API requests must be signed regardless of whether the requests are sent over HTTP or HTTPS. EBS implements symmetric encryption by using an AccessKey pair to verify the identity of the request sender. An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. They are the identity credentials issued by Alibaba Cloud. The AccessKey ID is used to verify the identity of the request sender, and the AccessKey secret is used to encrypt and verify the signature string. You must keep your AccessKey secret strictly confidential. For more information about how to obtain an AccessKey pair, see Obtain access credentials assigned by RAM. When you call an EBS API operation, you must perform the following steps to sign the request:
1. Create a canonicalized query string by arranging the request parameters.
i. Sort the request parameters. Sort the request parameters in alphabetical order. All **common request parameters** except **Signature** and all
**operation-specific request parameters** are included.

**Note**

If you use the GET method to send the request, these parameters are included in the request URI and connected by ampersands (**&** ). The first request parameter follows the question mark (**?**). ii. Encode the request parameters. Encode the name and value of each request parameter. The names and values must be URL encoded by using the UTF-8 character set based on the following rules: Uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, and specific special characters do not need to be encoded. The specific special characters are hyphens (-), underscores (_), periods (.), and tildes (~) Other characters must be percent encoded in the %XY format. XY represents the ASCII code of the characters in hexadecimal notation. For example, double quotation marks (") are encoded as %22. Extended UTF-8 characters must be encoded in the %XY%ZA… format. Spaces must be encoded as %20 instead of plus signs (+). This encoding method is similar to but slightly different from the `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` Multipurpose Internet Mail Extension (MIME) encoding algorithm, such as java.net.URLEncoder in the Java standard library. You can encode the parameter names and values by using the encoding method in the Java standard library. Then, in the encoded string, replace the plus signs (+) with %20, asterisks (*) with %2A, and tildes (~) with %7E to obtain an encoded string that complies with the preceding encoding rules. You can use the following percentEncode() method to perform the encoding:

| private static final String ENCODING = "UTF-8"; private static String percentEncode(String value) throws UnsupportedEncodingException { return value != null ? URLEncoder.encode(value, ENCODING).replace("+", "%20").replace("*", "%2A").replace("%7E", "~") : null; } |   |   |
|---|---|---|
| Use equal signs ( | = | ) to connect the encoded parameter names and values. |

iv. Sort the parameters in the order specified in Step 1.i and connect the parameter name-parameter value pairs by using ampersands (&) to generate a canonicalized query string.
2. Construct a string-to-sign based on the canonicalized query string and the following rules:

```
 StringToSign=
     HTTPMethod + "&" +
     percentEncode("/") + "&" +
      percentEncode(CanonicalizedQueryString)
```

HTTPMethod specifies the HTTP method that you want to use to send the request, such as GET. percentEncode("/") specifies the encoded value for the forward slash (/) based on the URL encoding rules described in Step 1.ii. The value is %2F. percentEncode(CanonicalizedQueryString) specifies the canonicalized query string generated in Step 1. The encoding follows the URL encoding rules described in Step 1.ii.
3. Calculate the Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) value of the string-to-sign as defined in RFC 2104.

**Note**

Use the SHA1 algorithm to calculate the HMAC value of the string-to-sign. The ******************** to which an ampersand (&) (ASCII:38) is appended is used as the key for HMAC calculation.
4. Encode the HMAC value in Base64 to obtain the signature string.
5. Add the signature string to the request as the **Signature** parameter. This way, the API request is signed.

**Note**

When the signature string is submitted to ECS as the final request parameter value, the value must be URL-encoded like other parameters based on rules defined in RFC 3986. API responses use the HTTP response format. A 2xx status code indicates a successful call, and a 4xx or 5xx status code indicates a failed call. Success responses can be returned in the JSON or XML format. You can specify the response format in the request. By default, responses are returned in the XML format.

**Note**

The sample responses provided in this topic have been formatted with line breaks and indentations for better readability. The actual responses are not properly formatted as these examples.

**Sample success responses**

XML format

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <!--Result root node--> <Operation name + Response>
    <!--Return request tag-->
    <RequestId>4C467B38-3910-447D-87BC-AC049166F216</RequestId>
    <!--Return result data-->
</Operation name + Response>
```

JSON format `{`

```json
    "RequestId": "4C467B38-3910-447D-87BC-AC049166F216",
    /* Return result data */
```

**Sample error responses**

If an error occurs when you call an API operation, no result data is returned. You can troubleshoot the error based on the error code returned. For an error that occurs when you call an API operation, a 4XX or 5XX HTTP status code is returned. The response body contains the specific error code and error message. The response body also contains the request ID and ID of the host that you wanted to access with this request. The request ID is globally unique. XML format

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <Error>
   <RequestId>8906582E-6722-409A-A6C4-0E7863B733A5</RequestId>
   <HostId>ebs.example.com</HostId>
   <Code>InvalidOwnerId</Code>
   <Message>The specified OwnerId is not valid.</Message>
</Error>
```

JSON format `{`

```json
    "RequestId": "8906582E-6722-409A-A6C4-0E7863B733A5",
    "HostId": "ebs.example.com",
    "Code": "InvalidOwnerId",
    "Message": "The specified OwnerId is not valid."
```

When you call API operations to access EBS resources within an Apsara Stack tenant account as a RAM user, EBS checks whether the RAM user is granted the required permissions.

**Background information**

You can use your Apsara Stack tenant account or a RAM user account to manage your EBS resources by using the EBS console or by calling API operations. Specific permissions are required in the following scenarios: A RAM user is newly created and does not have permissions to manage resources within the Apsara Stack tenant account. You want to access EBS resources from other Apsara Stack services, or access other Apsara Stack services from EBS. Before you can manage a resource that is configured with access control, you must be granted the required permissions on the resource and the relevant API operations by the resource owner. When an Apsara Stack tenant account requests access to EBS resources within your Apsara Stack tenant account by calling EBS API operations, EBS instructs RAM to perform a permission check to ensure that the requester account is granted the required permissions. Required permissions vary based on the requested EBS resources and API operations.

**Rule details**

The permissions that EBS checks vary based on the resources that are requested by the API operation and the syntax of the API operation. The following table describes the authentication rules for each API operation.

| API operation | Authentication rule | Description |
|---|---|---|
| CreateDisk | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:disk/* acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:snapshot/$snapshotid Note If you specify the SnapshotId parameter in the API request, you must specify the snapshotid variable. | Creates a disk. |
| DescribeDisks | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:disk/* | Queries one or more cloud disks and local disks that you have created. |
| AttachDisk | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:disk/$diskid acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:instance/$instanceid | Attaches a disk to an ECS instance. |
| DetachDisk | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:disk/$diskid acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:instance/$instanceid | Detaches a disk from an ECS instance. |
| ModifyDiskAttribute | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:disk/$diskid | Modifies the attributes of a cloud disk. |
| ReInitDisk | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:disk/$diskid | Re-initializes a cloud disk to the state that it was in when it was created. |
| ResetDisk | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:snapshot/$snapshotid acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:disk/$diskid | Rolls back a cloud disk to a specific point in time by using a snapshot of the cloud disk. |
| ReplaceSystemDisk | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:instance/$instanceId acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:image/$imageNo | Replaces the system disk or the operating system of an ECS instance. |
| ResizeDisk | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:disk/$diskId | Resizes a cloud disk. You can resize a system disk or a data disk. |
| DeleteDisk | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:disk/$diskid | Releases a disk. |
| CreateSnapshot | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:disk/$diskid acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:snapshot/* | Creates a snapshot for a cloud disk. |
| DescribeSnapshots | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:snapshot/$snapshotId acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:snapshot/* | Queries all the snapshots of an ECS instance or a cloud disk. |
| DeleteSnapshot | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:snapshot/$snapshotid | Deletes a specific snapshot. |
| DescribeSnapshotLinks | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:disk/$diskId acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:disk/* | Queries the snapshot chains of one or more cloud disks. |

| CreateAutoSnapshotPolicy | acs:ecs:*:$accountid:snapshot/* | Creates an automatic snapshot policy. |
|---|---|---|
| DeleteAutoSnapshotPolicy | acs:ecs:*:$accountid:snapshot/* | Deletes an automatic snapshot policy. |
| ModifySnapshotAttribute | acs:ecs:$regionid:$accountid:snapshot/$snapshotId | Modifies the name or description of a snapshot. |
| ApplyAutoSnapshotPolicy | acs:ecs:*:$accountid:snapshot/* | Applies an automatic snapshot policy to one or more cloud disks or replaces the existing automatic snapshot policy of the cloud disks. |
| CancelAutoSnapshotPolicy | acs:ecs:*:$accountid:snapshot/* | Disables an automatic snapshot policy for one or more cloud disks. |
| CreateDiskReplicaPair | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pair/* | Creates a replication pair. |
| StartDiskReplicaPair | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pair/$pairId | Enables the asynchronous replication feature for a replication pair. |
| DescribeDiskReplicaPairs | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pair/* | Queries the information of one or more replication pairs. |
| DescribeDiskReplicaPairProgress | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pair/$pairId | Queries the replication progress of a replication pair. |
| ModifyDiskReplicaPair | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pair/$pairId | Modifies the information of a replication pair. |
| FailoverDiskReplicaPair | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pair/$pairId | Enables the failover feature for a replication pair. |
| ReprotectDiskReplicaPair | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pair/$pairId | Enables the reverse replication feature for a replication pair. |
| StopDiskReplicaPair | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pair/$pairId | Disables the asynchronous replication feature for a replication pair. |
| DeleteDiskReplicaPair | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pair/$pairId | Deletes a replication pair. |
| CreateDiskReplicaGroup | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pg/* | Creates a replication pair- consistent group. |
| AddDiskReplicaPair | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pg/$groupId | Adds a replication pair to a replication pair-consistent group. |
| StartDiskReplicaGroup | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pg/$groupId | Enables the asynchronous replication feature for a replication pair-consistent group. |
| DescribeDiskReplicaGroups | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pg/* | Queries the information of one or more replication pair-consistent groups. |
| ModifyDiskReplicaGroup | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pg/$groupId | Modifies the information of a replication pair-consistent group. |
| FailoverDiskReplicaGroup | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pg/$groupId | Enables the failover feature for a replication pair-consistent group. |
| ReprotectDiskReplicaGroup | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pg/$groupId | Enables the reverse replication feature for a replication pair- consistent group. |
| RemoveDiskReplicaPair | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pg/$groupId | Removes a replication pair from a replication pair-consistent group. |
| StopDiskReplicaGroup | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pg/$groupId | Disables the asynchronous replication feature for a replication pair-consistent group. |
| DeleteDiskReplicaGroup | acs:ebs:$regionid:$accountid:pg/$groupId | Deletes a replication pair- consistent group. |

Common parameters include common request parameters, common headers, and common response parameters.

**Common request parameters**

Common request parameters must be included in all API requests. Table 1. Common request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Format | String | No | The format of the response. Set the value to JSON. |

| Version | String | Yes | The version number of the API. Specify the version number in the YYYY-MM-DD format. The version of the API varies based on the feature you want to use. If you want to use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, specify2 014-05- 26 as the API version. If you want to use the asynchronous replication or replication pair-consistent group feature, specify 2021-07-30 as the API version. |
|---|---|---|---|
| AccessKeyId | String | Yes | The AccessKey ID provided to you by Apsara Stack. |
| AccessKeySecret | String | Yes | The AccessKey secret provided to you by Apsara Stack. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | The region ID provided to you by Apsara Stack. |
| Product | String | Yes | The name of the service to which the API operation belongs. The version of the API varies based on the feature you want to use. If you want to use a feature related to cloud disks or snapshots, specifye cs as the service name. If you want to use the asynchronous replication or replication pair-consistent feature, specify ebs as the service name. |

To obtain the values of the `Product` and `Version` parameters in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, perform the following steps:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Others > API Tool**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **API Directory**.
4. In the **Search by operation name** search box, enter the name of an operation to query its information.

**Common headers**

| Header | Description |
|---|---|
| x-acs-organizationid | The ID of the organization in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For more information, seeO btain an organization ID. |
| x-acs-resourcegroupid | The ID of the resource set in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For more information, seeO btain a resource set ID. |
| x-acs-instanceid | The ID of the instance on which you want to perform the operation. For more information, seeO btain an instance ID. |

**Note**

When you call the API operations of cloud services, you must specify the **x-acs-instanceid**, **x-acs-organizationid**, and **x-acs-**
**resourcegroupid** headers. These headers specify the ID of the instance on which you want to perform the operation, and the organization and
resource set to which the instance belongs. If you call an API operation to create an instance or query the information about one or more instances, you do not need to specify the x-acs-instanceid header. If you do not specify the headers when you call an API operation, the information of the root organization and root resource set is used by default.

**Common response parameters**

API responses use the HTTP response format: A 2xx status code indicates a successful call. A 4xx or 5xx status code indicates a failed call. Responses are returned in the JSON format. Every response returns a unique request ID regardless of whether the call is successful. Creates a data disk. The disk can be an ultra disk, a shared ultra disk, a standard SSD, or a shared standard SSD. By default, the DeleteAutoSnapshot parameter is set to true when a disk is created. This indicates that when the disk is released, its automatic snapshots are deleted. You can call the ModifyDiskAttribute operation to modify this parameter. You must specify one of the Size and SnapshotId parameters. The Size parameter specifies the size of the disk and the SnapshotId parameter specifies the snapshot that is used to create the disk.
