Queries one or more Elastic Block Storage (EBS) devices that you created, including cloud disks and local disks. You can specify multiple request parameters such as `RegionId` , `ZoneId` , `DiskIds` , and `InstanceId` to be queried. Specified parameters have logical AND relations. Only the specified parameters are included in the filter conditions. The `DiskIds` value is a JSON array. If DiskIds is not specified, it is not used as a filter condition. If `DiskIds` is set to an empty JSON array, it is regarded as a valid filter condition, and an empty result is returned. A disk that has the multi-attach feature enabled can be attached to multiple instances. You can query the attach information of the disk based on the Attachment values in the response.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeDisks | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeDisks. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao-**** | The region ID of the disk. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| ZoneId | String | No | cn-qingdao-****-a | The zone ID of the disk. You can call the DescribeZones operation to query the most recent zone list. |
| DiskIds | String | No | ["d-bp67acfmxazb4p****", "d-bp67acfmxazb4p****", ... "d-bp67acfmxazb4p****"] | The IDs of disks. The value is a JSON array that consists of up to 100 disk IDs. Separate the disk IDs with commas (,). |
| InstanceId | String | No | i-bp67acfmxazb4p**** | The ID of the instance to which the disk is attached. |
| DiskType | String | No | all | The type of the disk. Valid values: all: system disk and data disk system: system disk data: data disk Default value: all. |
| Category | String | No | all | The category of the data disk. Valid values: cloudefficiency: ultra disk _ sanefficiency: shared ultra disk _ cloudssd: standard SSD _ sanssd: shared standard SSD _ cloudpperf: premium performance disk _ cloudsperf: standard performance disk _ Default value: cloudefficiency. _ |
| Status | String | No | All | The state of the cloud disk. Valid values: Inuse: The cloud disk is being used. _ Available: The cloud disk can be attached. Attaching: The cloud disk is being attached. Detaching: The cloud disk is being detached. Creating: The cloud disk is being created. ReIniting: The cloud disk is being initialized. All: All states. Default value: All. |
| SnapshotId | String | No | s-bp67acfmxazb4p**** | The ID of the snapshot used to create the cloud disk. |
| Portable | Boolean | No | false | Specifies whether the disk is removable. Valid values: true: The disk is removable. A removable disk can independently exist and can be attached to or detached from an instance within the same zone. false: The disk is not removable. A disk that is not removable cannot independently exist or be attached to or detached from an instance within the same zone. |
| DeleteWithInstance | Boolean | No | false | Specifies whether to release the cloud disk when its associated instance is released. Valid values: true: The cloud disk is released when its associated instance is released. false: The disk is not released but is retained when its attached instance is released. Default value: false. |
| DeleteAutoSnapshot | Boolean | No | false | Specifies whether to delete the automatic snapshots of the cloud disk when the disk is released. Valid values: true: The automatic snapshots of the cloud disk is deleted when the disk is released. false: The automatic snapshots of the cloud disk is not deleted when the disk is released. Default value: false. |
| PageNumber | Integer | No | 1 | The number of the page to return. Pages start from page 1. Default value: 1. |

| PageSize | Integer | No | 10 | The number of entries to return on each page. Maximum value: 100. Default value: 10. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NextToken | String | No | AAAAAdDWBF2**** | The query token. Set the value to the NextToken value returned in the last call to the DescribeDisks operation. |
| MaxResults | Integer | No | 50 | The maximum number of entries to return on each page. Valid values: 1 to 500. Default value: 10. |
| DiskName | String | No | test-DiskName | The name of the disk. |
| AutoSnapshotPolicyId | String | No | sp-m5e2w2jutw8bv31a**** | The ID of the automatic snapshot policy that is applied to the cloud disk. |
| EnableAutoSnapshot | Boolean | No | false | Specifies whether the automatic snapshot policy feature is enabled for the cloud disk. true: The automatic snapshot policy feature is enabled for the cloud disk. false: The automatic snapshot policy feature is disabled for the cloud disk. Note By default, the automatic snapshot policy feature is enabled for created cloud disks. You need to only apply an automatic snapshot policy to a cloud disk before you can use the automatic snapshot policy. |
| EnableAutomatedSnapshotPo licy | Boolean | No | false | Specifies whether to query disks that have automatic snapshot policies applied. true: queries disks that have automatic snapshot policies applied. false: does not query disks that have automatic snapshot policies applied. Default value: false. |
| Filter.1.Key | String | No | CreationStartTime | The key of filter 1 used to query resources. Set the value to CreationStartTime . You can specify a time by setting both Filter.1.Key and Filter.1.Value to query resources that were created after the time. |
| Filter.2.Key | String | No | CreationEndTime | The key of filter 2 used to query resources. Set the value to CreationEndTime . You can specify a time by setting both Filter.2.Key and Filter.2.Value to query resources that were created before the time. |
| Filter.1.Value | String | No | 2017-12-05T22:40:00Z | The value of filter 1 used to query resources. Set the value to a time. If you specify this parameter, you must also specify the Filter.1.Key parameter. Specify the time in the yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mmZ format. The time must be in UTC. |
| Filter.2.Value | String | No | 2017-12-06T22:40:00Z | The value of filter 2 used to query resources. Set the value to a time. If you specify this parameter, you must also specify the Filter.2.Key parameter. Specify the time in the yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mmZ format. The time must be in UTC. |
| EnableShared | Boolean | No | false | Specifies whether the disk is a Shared Block Storage device. Valid values: true false Default value: false. |
| Encrypted | Boolean | No | false | Specifies whether to query only encrypted cloud disks. Valid values: true: queries only encrypted cloud disks. false: does not query encrypted cloud disks. Default value: false. |

| DryRun | Boolean | No | false | Specifies whether to check the validity of the request without actually making the request. Attaches a system disk or data disk to an instance. The instance and the disk must reside in the same zone. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: The disk to be attached must be in the **Unattached** ( `Available` ) state. When the disk is attached as a data disk, take note of the following items: The instance must be in the **Running** ( `Running` ) or **Stopped** ( `Stopped` ) state. When the disk is attached as a system disk, take note of the following items: The instance must be the original instance from which the system disk is detached. The instance must be in the **Stopped** ( `Stopped` ) state. The logon credentials must be configured. When you query the instance information and the responses contain `{"OperationLocks": {"LockReason" : "security"}}` , the instance is locked for security reasons and all operations cannot take effect on the instance.

| DiskId | String | Yes | d-bp198f7xn673w2rw**** | The ID of the disk to be attached. The disk specified by the DiskId parameter and the instance specified by the InstanceId parameter must reside in the same zone. Note For more information about the limits on attaching a data disk and system disk, see the "Description" section of this topic. |
| InstanceId | String | Yes | i-bp1ahcvgu9z55pk7**** | The ID of the instance to which to attach the disk. |
| Device | String | No | testName | The device name of the disk. Note This parameter will be removed in the future. We recommend that you use other parameters to ensure future compatibility. |

| DeleteWithInstance | Boolean | No | false | Specifies whether to release the disk along with the instance to which it is attached. Valid values: true: releases the disk when the instance is released. false: does not release the disk when the instance is released. Default value: false. Note If OperationLocks in the DescribeInstances response contains "LockReason" : "security" for the instance to which the disk is attached, the instance is locked for security reasons. You can call this operation to detach a data disk or system disk from an instance. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: The disk to be detached must be in the Running ( `In_Use` ) state. The instance from which you want to detach a data disk must be in the **Running** ( `Running` ) or **Stopped** ( `Stopped` ) state. The instance from which you want to detach the system disk must be in the **Stopped** ( `Stopped` ) state.

| {"OperationLocks": | {"LockReason" : "security"}} |
|---|---|

locked for security reasons and all operations are prohibited on it. DetachDisk is an asynchronous operation. It takes about one minute for the disk to be detached after this operation is called.

| DiskId | String | Yes | d-bp67acfmxazb4p**** | The ID of the disk to be detached. |
| InstanceId | String | Yes | i-bp67acfmxazb4p**** | The ID of the instance from which the disk is to be detached. |
| DeleteWithInstance | Boolean | No | false | The automatic release attribute of the system disk. That is, this parameter specifies whether the system disk is released when its attached instance is released. Valid values: true: The system disk is released when its attached instance is released. false: The system disk is not released but is retained when its attached instance is released. Default value: true. Note If a data disk is to be detached, the default value is false . |

You can call this operation to modify the attributes of one or more Block Storage devices, including their names, descriptions, and whether they are released along with their attached instances. If you set DeleteWithInstance to false for a disk and the instance to which the disk is attached is locked for security reasons, the DeleteWithInstance parameter will be ignored and the disk will be released along with the instance. (If the value of `LockReason` is security in OperationLocks of the API response when you query information of an instance, the instance is locked for security reasons.)

Re-initializes a disk. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: The disk to be re-initialized must be in the **In Use** (In_use) state and the instance to which the disk is attached must be in the **Stopped** (Stopped) state. If the instance has never been started since it was created, the disks attached to it cannot be re-initialized. When a system disk is re-initialized, it is restored to the state of the image from which it was created. If the image has been deleted, the disk cannot be re-initialized. When a separately created data disk is re-initialized, it is restored to an empty data disk. When a data disk that was created from a snapshot is re-initialized, the disk is restored to the state of the snapshot. If the snapshot has been deleted, the disk cannot be re-initialized and an error is returned.

| DiskId | String | Yes | d-bp67acfmxazb4p**** | The ID of the disk. |
| Password | String | No | EcsV587! | Specifies whether to reset the password of the instance when you re-initialize its system disk. The password must be 8 to 30 characters in length and contain at least three of the following character types: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, and special characters. Special characters include: ()`~!@#$%^&*-_+=\|{}[]:;'<>,.?/ For Windows instances, the password cannot start with a forward slash (/). Note For security reasons, we recommend that you use HTTPS to send requests if the Password parameter is specified. |
| KeyPairName | String | No | test-KeyPairName | The name of the key pair. Note The parameter is applicable only to Linux instances. You can bind an SSH key pair to an instance as the logon credential when you re-initialize its system disk. After the SSH key pair is bound, the username and password logon method is disabled for the instance. |
| AutoStartInstance | Boolean | No | true | Specifies whether to automatically start the instance after the disk is re-initialized. Default value: false. |
| SecurityEnhancementStrateg y | String | No | Active | Specifies whether to use Security Center after the system disk is re-initialized. Valid values: Active: uses Security Center after the system disk is re- initialized. This value is applicable only to public images. Deactive: does not use Security Center after the system disk is re-initialized. This value is applicable to all images. Default value: Deactive. |

Restores a disk to a specific point in time from a snapshot of the disk. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: The disk must be in the In Use (In_Use) state. The instance to which the disk is attached must be in the Stopped (Stopped) state. The snapshot specified by the SnapshotId parameter must be created from the disk specified by the DiskId parameter. When you call the DescribeInstances operation to query the instance information and the responses contain `{"OperationLocks": {"LockReason" :` `"security"}}` , the instance is locked for security reasons and all operations cannot take effect on the instance.

| SnapshotId | String | Yes | s-bp1btgnlb4licd41**** | The ID of the snapshot that is used to restore the disk. |

You can call this operation to replace the system disk or operating system of an ECS instance. After the system disk is replaced, the ID of the system disk changes and the original disk is released. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: You cannot change the category of the system disk. The instance to which the system disk to be replaced is attached must be in the Stopped (Stopped) state. If OperationLocks in the DescribeInstances response contains "LockReason" : "security" for an instance, the instance is locked for security reasons and cannot be restarted. You can use the SystemDisk.Size parameter to specify the capacity of the new system disk.

| ImageId | String | No | m-bp67acfmxazb4p**** | The ID of the image to be used to replace the system disk. |
| SystemDisk.Size | Integer | No | 80 | The capacity of the new system disk. Unit: GiB. Valid values: Max{20, the size of the image specified by ImageId} to 500. Default value: 40 or the size of the specified image, whichever is greater. |
| ClientToken | String | No | 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456- 426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request You can use the client to generate the value, but you must make sure that it is unique among different requests. The ClientToken value can only contain ASCII characters and cannot exceed 64 characters in length. For more information, see How to ensure idempotence in ECS Developer Guide. |
| UseAdditionalService | Boolean | No | true | Specifies whether to use the virtual machine system configuration provided by Apsara Stack (Windows: NTP and KMS. Linux: NTP and YUM). Note This parameter takes effect only when you attach a system disk, whose device name is /dev/xvda. |
| Password | String | No | EcsV587! | The new password of the instance. The password must be 8 to 30 characters in length. It must include at least three of the following character types: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, and special characters. Special characters include: ( ) ` ~ ! @ # $ % ^ & * - _ + = \| { } [ ] : ; ' < > , . ? / The password of a Windows instance cannot start with a forward slash (/). This parameter is empty by default, which indicates that the current password remains unchanged. Note If the Password parameter is specified, we recommend that you send requests over HTTPS to avoid password leaks. |

You can call this operation to resize a system disk or data disk.

| Note Before you call this operation to resize a disk, you must check the partition format of the disk. You cannot resize an MBR disk to larger than 2 TiB in size without data loss. To resize an MBR disk to larger than 2 TiB in size, we recommend that you create and attach a new data disk with the desired size. Then, we recommend that you use the GPT partition format to partition and format the new data disk and copy data from the MBR-formatted data disk to the new GPT-formatted data disk. For more information, see Expand a disk in ECS User Guide. |   |   |   |   |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| You can resize the disks of different categories, including basic disks ( | cloud | ), ultra disks | ( cloud_efficiency | ), and standard SSDs ( | cloud_ssd | ). |

You cannot resize a disk when a snapshot is being created for the disk. The instance to which the disk to be resized is attached must be in the **Running** ( `Running` ) or **Stopped** ( `Stopped` ) state. After you resize a disk, its partitions and file systems are not changed. You must manually allocate the storage space on the disk after it is resized.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | ResizeDisk | The operation that you want to perform. If you use a custom HTTP URL or HTTPS URL to make an API request, you must specify the Action parameter. Set the value to ResizeDisk. |
| DiskId | String | Yes | d-bp67acfmxazb4p**** | The ID of the disk. |
| NewSize | Integer | Yes | 1900 | The new disk capacity. Unit: GiB. Valid values: For ultra disks (cloudefficiency): 20 to 32768 _ For standard SSDs (cloudefficiency): 20 to 32768 _ For basic disks (cloud): 5 to 2000 The new disk capacity must be greater than the original disk capacity. |
| Type | String | No | offline | The method used to resize the disk. Default value: offline. Valid values: offline: resizes the disk offline. After you resize a disk offline, you must restart its associated instance by using the ECS console or by calling the RebootInstance operation to make the resizing operation take effect. online: resizes the disk online. After you resize a disk online, the operation takes effect immediately without the need to restart the instance. You can resize ultra disks and standard SSDs online. |
| ClientToken | String | No | 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456- 426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request You can use the client to generate the value, but you must make sure that it is unique among different requests. The ClientToken value can only contain ASCII characters and cannot exceed 64 characters in length. For more information, see How to ensure idempotence in ECS Developer Guide. |

| RequestId | String | F3CD6886-D8D0-4FEE-B93E- 1B73239673DE | The ID of the request. |

Releases a data disk. When you call this operation to release a data disk, take note of the following items: Manual snapshots of the disk are retained. You can call the ModifyDiskAttribute operation to configure whether to retain automatic snapshots of the disk or release them along with the disk. We recommend that you delete the snapshots that are no longer needed to maintain a sufficient quota for new automatic snapshots. The disk must be in the Unattached (Available) state. If the specified DiskId parameter does not exist, the request is ignored.

Creates a snapshot for a disk. In the following scenarios, snapshots cannot be created for a disk: The number of manual snapshots of the disk has reached 256. A snapshot is being created for the disk. The Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance to which the disk is attached has never been started. The instance to which the disk is attached is not in the **Stopped** ( `Stopped` ) or **Running** ( `Running` ) state. If the response contains `{"OperationLocks": {"LockReason" : "security"}}` when you query the information of the instance, the instance is locked for security reasons and all operations are prohibited on it. When you create a snapshot, take note of the following items: About 1 hour after an instance is created or the system disk of an instance is replaced, you can create a snapshot for a disk that is attached to the instance. After a data disk is attached to an instance, you must wait a period of time before you can create a snapshot for the data disk. The amount of time to wait depends on the volume of data stored on the disk. If a snapshot is being created, this snapshot cannot be used to create a custom image by calling the CreateImage operation. If the disk for which you want to create a snapshot is attached to an ECS instance, do not change the instance state during snapshot creation.

It can contain letters, digits, colons (:), underscores (), and hyphens (-). _ It cannot start with auto because snapshots whose names start with auto are recognized as automatic snapshots. |

Deletes a snapshot. If you call this operation to delete a snapshot that is being created, the associated snapshot creation task is also canceled. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: If the specified snapshot does not exist, the request is ignored. A snapshot that has already been used to create custom images cannot be deleted. You must call the DeleteImage operation to delete the custom images before you can delete the snapshot. If the specified snapshot has been used to create disks and the `Force` parameter is not specified or is set to `false` , the snapshot cannot be deleted directly. If you want to delete the snapshot, set the `Force` parameter to true to forcefully delete the snapshot. The disks created from the snapshot cannot be re-initialized after the snapshot is forcefully deleted.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DeleteSnapshot | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DeleteSnapshot. |
| SnapshotId | String | Yes | s-bp1btgnlb4licd41**** | The ID of the snapshot. You can call the DescribeSnapshots operation to query the snapshot ID. |
| Force | Boolean | No | false | Specifies whether to forcefully delete the snapshot that has been used to create disks. Valid values: true: forcefully deletes the snapshot. After the snapshot is forcefully deleted, the disks created from this snapshot cannot be re-initialized. false: does not forcefully delete the snapshot. Default value: false. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F-4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE3**** | The ID of the request. Every response returns a unique request ID regardless of whether the call is successful. |

You can call this operation to query the snapshot chains of one or more disks. A snapshot chain is a chain of all the snapshots created for a disk. A disk corresponds to a chain of snapshots. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: You can specify multiple request parameters such as `RegionId` , `DiskIds` , and `InstanceId` to be queried. Specified parameters have logical AND relations. Only the specified parameters are used as filter conditions. If the `DiskIds` and `SnapshotLinkIds` parameters are set to empty JSON arrays, they are regarded as valid filter conditions and an empty result is returned.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeSnapshotLinks | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeSnapshotLinks. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao-env17-d01 | The region ID of the disk. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| InstanceId | String | No | i-bp1ahcvgu9z55pk7**** | The ID of the instance. |
| DiskIds | String | No | ["d-bp198f7xn673w2rw****", "d-bp12te2l9m0170wc****", ... "d-bp1btgnlb4lgdzoi****"] | The IDs of disks. The value is a JSON array that consists of up to 100 disk IDs. Separate multiple disk IDs with commas (,). |
| SnapshotLinkIds | String | No | ["sl-bp14r3b4xczuenhr****", "sl-bp1eftye2796vi2a****", ... "sl-bp1aixnfbjo290a8****"] | The IDs of snapshot chains. The value is a JSON array that consists of up to 100 snapshot chain IDs. Separate multiple snapshot chain IDs with commas (,). |
| PageNumber | Integer | No | 1 | The number of the page to return. Pages start from page 1. Default value: 1. |
| PageSize | Integer | No | 50 | The number of entries to return on each page. Valid values: 1 to 100. Default value: 10. |

**Response parameters**

| SnapshotLinks | Array of SnapshotLink |   | Details about the snapshot chains. |
| SnapshotLink |   |   |   |
| Category | String | test | Note This parameter is not supported. |
| InstanceId | String | i-bp1ahcvgu9z55pk7**** | The ID of the instance. |
| InstanceName | String | test-InstanceName | The name of the instance. |
| RegionId | String | cn-qingdao-env17-d01 | The ID of the region where the source disk of the snapshot chain is located. |
| SnapshotLinkId | String | sl-bp14r3b4xczuenhr**** | The ID of the snapshot chain. |
| SourceDiskId | String | d-bp198f7xn673w2rw**** | The ID of the source disk. This parameter is retained even if the source disk is deleted. |
| SourceDiskName | String | test-SourceDiskName | The name of the source disk. |

You can call this operation to create an automatic snapshot policy. After an automatic snapshot policy is created, you can call the ApplyAutoSnapshotPolicy operation to apply the policy to disks. You can also call the ModifyAutoSnapshotPolicyEx operation to modify the automatic snapshot policy. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: A maximum of 100 automatic snapshot policies can be created in each region per Apsara Stack tenant account. If an automatic snapshot is being created when the time scheduled for a new automatic snapshot is due, the new snapshot task is skipped. This may occur when a disk contains a large volume of data. For example, an automatic snapshot policy is applied to a disk that contains a large volume of data, and the policy specifies that snapshots are created at 09:00, 10:00, 11:00, and 12:00. The system starts to create a snapshot for the disk at 09:00. The snapshot creation process takes 80 minutes and ends at 10:20. The system skips the automatic snapshot task scheduled for 10:00 and creates the next automatic snapshot for the disk at 11:00.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | CreateAutoSnapshotPolicy | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to CreateAutoSnapshotPolicy. |
| regionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao-env17-d01 | The ID of the region in which to create an automatic snapshot policy. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| repeatWeekdays | String | Yes | ["1","2"] | The days of the week on which to create automatic snapshots. Valid values: 1 to 7, which correspond to Monday to Sunday. 1 indicates Monday. To schedule multiple automatic snapshots to be created for a disk in a week, you can set this parameter to a JSON array. You can specify up to seven values in the array. Separate the values in the array with commas (,). Example: ["1","2"..." "7"] . |
| retentionDays | Integer | Yes | 30 | The number of days for which to retain automatic snapshots. Valid values: -1: Automatic snapshots are permanently retained. 1 to 65535: Automatic snapshots are retained for a specified number of days. Default value: -1. |
| timePoints | String | Yes | ["0", "1", … "23"] | The point in time at which to create automatic snapshots. Unit: hours. Valid values: 0 to 23. These values correspond to the hours of the day from 00:00 to 23:00. 1 indicates 01:00. To schedule multiple automatic snapshots to be created for a disk in a day, you can set this parameter to a JSON array that consists of multiple values. You can specify up to 24 values in the array. |
| autoSnapshotPolicyName | String | No | test- autoSnapshotPolicyName | The name of the automatic snapshot policy. The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length and can contain letters, digits, colons (:), underscores (), and hyphens (-). The name must _ start with a letter and cannot start with http:// or https://. This parameter is empty by default. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| AutoSnapshotPolicyId | String | sp-bp12m37ccmxvbmi5**** | The ID of the automatic snapshot policy. |
| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F-4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE3C83E | The ID of the request. |

Applies an automatic snapshot policy to one or more disks. If you apply an automatic snapshot policy to a disk that already has an automatic snapshot policy, the new policy replaces the original policy to take effect on the disk. Each disk can have only one automatic snapshot policy applied. A single automatic snapshot policy can be applied to multiple disks.

Creates a snapshot-consistent group for the disks in an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance. A snapshot-consistent group can contain snapshots of one or more disks. When you call this operation, take note of the following items:

| Available ) | state. |
|---|---|
| he Running | ( Running |

The disk for which you want to create a snapshot must be in the **Running** ( `Running` ) or **Unattached** ( `Available` ) state. If the disk is in the **Running** ( `Running` ) state, the instance to which the disk is attached must be in the **Running** ( `Running` ) or **Stopped** ( `Stopped` ) state. If the disk is in the **Unattached** ( `Available` ) state, make sure that the disk has been attached to an ECS instance. Snapshots cannot be created for disks that have never been attached to ECS instances. The snapshot-consistent group feature can be used to create snapshots only for premium performance disks and standard performance disks. A single snapshot-consistent group can contain snapshots of up to 16 disks including system disks and data disks and cannot exceed 32 TiB in size. Snapshots that you created are retained until they are deleted. We recommend that you delete unnecessary snapshots on a regular basis to prevent the number of snapshots from exceeding the quota. Snapshot-consistent groups cannot be created for disks that have the multi-attach feature enabled. If disks that have the multi-attach feature enabled are attached to an instance, you must set the `ExcludeDiskId.N` parameter to exclude these disks. For more information about the snapshot-consistent group feature, see Creating a snapshot-consistent group in ECS User Guide.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | CreateSnapshotGroup | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to CreateSnapshotGroup. |
| InstanceId | String | Yes | i-q1a01ac6ae3gcb11**** | The ID of the instance. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao-**** | The region ID of the instance. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. For more information, see DescribeRegions in ECS Developer Guide. |
| ExcludeDiskId.N | RepeatList | No | d-q1a0113yyonhqbgu**** | The ID of disk N for which you do not need to create snapshots. After this parameter is specified, the created snapshot-consistent group does not contain snapshots of the disk. Valid values of N: 1 to 16. This parameter is empty by default, which indicates that snapshots are created for all disks in the instance. |
| InstantAccess | Boolean | No | false | Specifies whether to enable the instant access feature. Valid values: true: enables the instant access feature. false: disables the instant access feature. Default value: false. |
| InstantAccessRetentionDays | Integer | No | 1 | The number of days for which the instant access feature is available. Unit: days. Valid values: 1 to 65535. This parameter takes effect only when InstantAccess is set to true. The instant access feature is automatically disabled when the specified duration of instant access expires. This parameter is empty by default, which indicates that the expiration time of the instant access feature is determined by the time when snapshots are released. |
| Name | String | No | testName | The name of the snapshot-consistent group. The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, periods (.), underscores (), hyphens (-), and colons (:). _ It must start with a letter or a digit and cannot start with http:// or https:// . |
| Description | String | No | This is description. | The description of the snapshot-consistent group. The description must be 2 to 256 characters in length and cannot start with http:// or https:// . |

|---|---|---|---|

| SnapshotGroupId | String | 01ABBD93-1ABB-4D92-B496- 1A3D20EC**** | The ID of the request. |

Creates a replication pair. The asynchronous replication feature can be used to protect data across zones in a region based on the data replication capability of EBS. This feature can be used to asynchronously replicate data from a disk in a zone of a region to a disk in another zone of the region for disaster recovery. You can use this feature to implement disaster recovery for critical business to protect data in your databases and improve business continuity. Before you call this operation, take note of the following items: Make sure that the primary disk and secondary disk for disaster recovery are prepared. The secondary disk cannot be deployed in the same zone as the primary disk. After you call this operation to create a replication pair between the primary disk and the secondary disk, you must call the StartDiskReplicaPair operation to enable asynchronous replication for the replication pair. Then, data can be periodically replicated from the primary disk to the secondary disk across zones in the same region.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | CreateDiskReplicaPair | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to CreateDiskReplicaPair. |

| DestinationDiskId | String | Yes | d-sa1f82p58p1tdw9g**** | The ID of the secondary disk. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DestinationRegionId | String | Yes | cn-beijing | The ID of the region in which the secondary disk is deployed. |
| DestinationZoneId | String | Yes | cn-beijing-e | The ID of the zone in which the secondary disk is deployed. |
| DiskId | String | Yes | d-iq80sgp4d0xbk24q**** | The ID of the primary disk. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-beijing | The ID of the region in which the replication pair is deployed. |
| SourceZoneId | String | Yes | cn-beijing-f | The ID of the zone in which the primary disk is deployed. |
| PairName | String | No | TestReplicaPair | The name of the replication pair. The name must meet the following requirements: The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length. The name must start with a letter and cannot start with http:// or https:// . The name can contain letters, digits, colons (:), underscores (), periods (.), and hyphens (-). _ |
| Description | String | No | This is description. | The description of the replication pair. The description must be 2 to 256 characters in length and cannot start with http:// or https:// . |
| ClientToken | String | No | 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456- 426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request. You can use the client to generate the value, but you must make sure that the value is unique among different requests. The token is a string of up to 64 ASCII characters. For more information, see How to ensure idempotence. |

Enables the asynchronous replication feature for a replication pair to periodically replicate data from the primary disk to the secondary disk across regions. If you want to perform an automatic synchronization by setting the OneShot parameter to false, make sure that the replication pair is in the **created**,
**initial_syncing**, **syncing**, **normal**, or **stopped** state and is not added to a replication pair-consistent group.
If you want to perform manual synchronization by setting the OneShot parameter to true, make sure that the replication pair is in the **created**,
**manual_syncing**, or **stopped** state and is not added to a replication pair-consistent group.
After you enable the asynchronous replication feature for a replication pair, the replication pair enters the **initial_syncing** state. The system performs the first asynchronous replication to replicate all data from the primary disk to the secondary disk.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | StartDiskReplicaPair | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to StartDiskReplicaPair. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-beijing | The region ID of the primary or secondary disk in the replication pair. You can call the DescribeDiskReplicaPairs operation to query the region information of replication pairs. |
| ReplicaPairId | String | Yes | pair-cn-dsa**** | The ID of the replication pair. |
| ClientToken | String | No | 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456- 426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request. You can use the client to generate the value, but you must make sure that the value is unique among different requests. The token is a string of up to 64 ASCII characters. For more information, see How to ensure idempotence. |
| OneShot | Boolean | No | true | Specifies whether to immediately synchronize data. Valid values: true: immediately synchronizes data. false: synchronizes data based on the RPO of the replication pair-consistent group. This is the default value. |

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | A37597A6-BB99-19B3-85EA- 4C2B91F00123 | The ID of the request. |

Queries the information of one or more replication pairs in a region. When you call this operation for a specific region, if the primary or secondary disk of a replication pair is located within the region, the information of the replication pair is contained in the response. We recommend that you use the MaxResults and NextToken parameters for a paged query. During a paged query, when you call the DescribeDiskReplicaPairs operation to retrieve the first page of results, set MaxResults to specify the maximum number of entries to return in the call. The return value of NextToken is a pagination token, which can be used in the next call to retrieve a new page of results. When you call the DescribeDiskReplicaPairs operation to retrieve a new page of results, set NextToken to the NextToken value returned in the previous call and set MaxResults to specify the maximum number of entries to return in this call.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeDiskReplicaPairs | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeDiskReplicaPairs. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-beijing | The region ID of the primary disk in the replication pair. |
| MaxResults | Long | No | 1 | The maximum number of entries to return on each page. Valid values: 1 to 500. Default value: 10. |
| NextToken | String | No | AAAAAdDWBF2**** | The query token. Set the value to the NextToken value returned in the previous call to the DescribeDiskReplicaPairs operation. Leave this parameter empty the first time you call this operation. |

| PairIds | String | No | pair-cn-dsa****,pair-cn- asd**** | The IDs of the replication pairs. You can specify the IDs of one or more replication pairs. Separate the IDs with commas (,). This parameter is empty by default, which indicates that all replication pairs in the specified region are queried. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Site | String | No | production | The type of the site from which the information of replication pairs is queried. If the Site parameter is not specified, information such as the state of replication pairs at the primary site is queried and returned. Otherwise, information such as the state of replication pairs at the site specified by the Site parameter is queried and returned. Valid values: production: primary site backup: secondary site |
| ReplicaGroupId | String | No | pg-myreplica**** | The ID of the replication pair-consistent group. If you specify a replication pair-consistent group, the information of the replication pairs in the group is contained in the response. If you set the ReplicaGroupId parameter to a hyphen (-), the information of the replication pairs that do not belong to any replication pair-consistent group is contained in the response. |

After you create a replication pair and enable asynchronous replication for the replication pair, the replication pair is in this state the first time data is synchronized from the primary disk to the secondary disk. manualsyncing: Data is being manually synchronized between the _ disks. Enables the failover feature for a replication pair. When the primary disk in a replication pair fails, you can call this operation to enable the read and write permissions on the secondary disk. The replication pair must be in the **manual_syncing**, **syncing**, **normal**, **stopping**, **stop_failed**, **stopped**, **failovering**, **failover_failed**, or

After a failover is performed, the replication pair enters the **failovered** state.

Enables the reverse replication feature for a replication pair. After you enable the reverse replication feature, the direction of data replication is inverted. Data is replicated from the original secondary disk to the original primary disk. The replication pair must be in the **failovered**, **reprotecting**, or **reprotect_failed** state and not be added to any replication pair-consistent group. The primary disk must be detached from its associated ECS instance and is in the Unattached state. You can call the DetachDisk operation to detach disks. After you enable the reverse replication feature, you must call the StartDiskReplicaPair operation again to enable the replication pair before data can be replicated from the original secondary disk to the original primary disk.

| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-shanghai | The region ID of the secondary disk in the replication pair. You can call the DescribeDiskReplicaPairs operation to obtain the region information of secondary disks in replication pairs. Note The reverse replication feature must be enabled from the region in which the secondary disk is located. |
| ReplicaPairId | String | Yes | pair-cn-dsa**** | The ID of the replication pair. |
| ClientToken | String | No | 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456- 426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request. You can use the client to generate a client token. Stops a replication pair. The replication pair must be in the **initial_syncing**, **manual_syncing**, **syncing**, **normal**, **stopping**, **stopping_failed**, or **stopped** state and not be added to any replication pair-consistent group. After you stop a replication pair, the replication pair enters the **stopped** state. The secondary disk rolls back to the point in time when the last asynchronous replication was complete and drops all the data that is being replicated from the primary disk. If you stop a replication pair that is in the **initial_syncing** state and then perform a failover, an error is returned.

Deletes a replication pair. The replication pair must be in the **creating**, **created**, **create_failed**, **stopped**, **failovered**, **deleting**, **delete_failed**, or **invalid** state. This operation deletes only replication pairs. The primary and secondary disks in the deleted replication pairs are retained. To delete a replication pair, you must call this operation in the region in which the primary disk is located. After the replication pair is deleted, functionality limits are lifted from the primary and secondary disks. For example, you can attach the secondary disk, resize the disk, or read data from or write data to the disk. The request initiated by calling this operation will be successful even if you specify a replication pair ID that does not exist or is invalid.

Creates a replication pair-consistent group. A replication pair-consistent group is a combination of multiple replication pairs that replicate data in the same direction. A replication pair-consistent group allows you to start or stop multiple replication pairs, perform failovers for multiple replication pairs, or enable the reverse replication feature for multiple replication pairs at a time. When you create a replication pair-consistent group, take note of the following items: Replication pair-consistent groups support disaster recovery across zones within the same region. A replication pair and a replication pair-consistent group replicate data in the same direction if they have the same primary region (production region), primary zone (production zone), secondary region (disaster recovery region), and secondary zone (disaster recovery zone). Replication pairs can be added to only a replication pair-consistent group that replicates data in the same direction as them. After replication pairs are added to a replication pair-consistent group, the recovery point objective (RPO) of the group takes effect on the pairs in place of their original RPOs.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | CreateDiskReplicaGroup | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to CreateDiskReplicaGroup. |
| DestinationRegionId | String | Yes | cn-shanghai | The ID of the region in which the secondary site is deployed. |
| DestinationZoneId | String | Yes | cn-shanghai-e | The ID of the zone in which the secondary site is deployed. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-hangzhou | The ID of the region in which you want to create the replication pair-consistent group. The primary site is deployed in this region. The value of this parameter is also the identifier and a component of Endpoint, as shown in the following sample request. |
| SourceZoneId | String | Yes | cn-beijing-f | The ID of the zone in which the primary site is deployed. |

Adds a replication pair to a replication pair-consistent group. A replication pair and a replication pair-consistent group replicate data in the same direction if they have the same primary region (production region), primary zone (production zone), secondary region (disaster recovery region), and secondary zone (disaster recovery zone). Replication pairs can be added to only a replication pair-consistent group that replicates data in the same direction as them. Up to 256 replication pairs can be added to a single replication pair-consistent group. Before you add a replication pair to a replication pair-consistent group, make sure that the pair and the group are in the **created** or **stopped** state.

Enables the asynchronous replication feature for the replication pairs in a replication pair-consistent group. After you enable the asynchronous replication feature, the system first performs a full synchronization to synchronize all data from the primary disks to the secondary disks and then periodically synchronizes incremental data based on the RPO of the replication pair-consistent group. If you want to perform automatic synchronization by setting the OneShot parameter to false, make sure that the replication pair-consistent group is in the **created**, **syncing**, **normal**, or **stopped** state. If you want to perform manual synchronization by setting the OneShot parameter to true, make sure the replication pair-consistent group is in the
**created**, **manual_syncing**, or **stopped** state.
After you enable the asynchronous replication feature for a replication pair-consistent group, the group enters the **initial_syncing** state. The system performs the first asynchronous replication to replicate all data from the primary disks to the secondary disks.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | StartDiskReplicaGroup | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to StartDiskReplicaGroup. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-beijing | The region ID of the replication pair-consistent group. The value of this parameter is also the identifier and a component of Endpoint, as shown in the following sample request. |
| ReplicaGroupId | String | Yes | pg-myreplica**** | The ID of the replication pair-consistent group. |
| ClientToken | String | No | 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456- 426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request. You can use the client to generate the value, but you must make sure that the value is unique among different requests. The token is a string of up to 64 ASCII characters. For more information, see How to ensure idempotence. |
| OneShot | Boolean | No | true | Specifies whether to immediately synchronize data. Valid values: true: immediately synchronizes data. false: synchronizes data based on the RPO of the replication pair-consistent group. This is the default value. |

Queries the information of one or more replication pair-consistent groups in a region. We recommend that you use the MaxResults and NextToken parameters for a paged query. During a paged query, when you call the DescribeDiskReplicaGroups operation to retrieve the first page of results, set MaxResults to specify the maximum number of entries to return in the call. The return value of NextToken is a pagination token, which can be used in the next call to retrieve a new page of results. When you call the DescribeDiskReplicaGroups operation to retrieve a new page of results, set NextToken to the NextToken value returned in the previous call and set MaxResults to specify the maximum number of entries to return in this call.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeDiskReplicaGroups | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeDiskReplicaGroups. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-beijing | The region ID of the replication pair-consistent group. The value of this parameter is also the identifier and a component of Endpoint, as shown in the following sample request. |
| MaxResults | Long | No | 10 | The maximum number of entries to return on each page. Valid values: 1 to 500. Default value: 10. |
| NextToken | String | No | AAAAAdDWBF2**** | The query token. Set the value to the NextToken value returned in the previous call to the DescribeDiskReplicaGroups operation. Leave this parameter empty the first time you call this operation. |
| GroupIds | String | No | pg-cn-dsa****,pg-cn-asd****` | The IDs of the replication pair-consistent groups. You can specify the IDs of one or more replication pair-consistent groups. Separate the IDs with commas (,). This parameter is empty by default, which indicates that all replication pair-consistent groups in the specified region are queried. |
| Site | String | No | production | The type of the site from which the information of replication pair-consistent groups is queried. This parameter is used for scenarios where data is replicated across zones by using replication pairs. If the Site parameter is not specified, information such as the state of replication pair-consistent groups at the primary site is queried and returned. Otherwise, information such as the state of replication pair- consistent groups at the site specified by the Site parameter is queried and returned. Valid values: production: primary site backup: secondary site |

| DestinationZoneId | String | cn-shanghai-e | The ID of the zone in which the secondary site is deployed. |

This state indicates that specific replication pairs in the replication pair- consistent group are abnormal. creating: The replication pair-consistent group is being created. created: The replication pair-consistent group is created. createfailed: The replication pair-consistent group cannot be _ created. manualsyncing: Data is being manually synchronized between the _ disks in the replication pair-consistent group. When data is being asynchronously replicated from the primary disks to the secondary disks not for the first time, the replication pair-consistent group is in this state. normal: The replication pair-consistent group is working normally. Enables the failover feature for the replication pairs in a replication pair-consistent group. When the primary disks of specific replication pairs in a replication pair-consistent group fail, you can call this operation to enable the read and write permissions on the secondary disks. The replication pair-consistent group must be in the **manual_syncing**, **syncing**, **normal**, **stopping**, **stop_failed**, **stopped**, **failovering**,
**failover_failed**, or **failovered** state.
After a failover is performed, the replication pair-consistent group enters the **failovered** state. Before you perform a failover, make sure that the first full data synchronization is complete between the primary site and the secondary site.

|---|---|---|---|---|

| ClientToken | String | No | 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456- 426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request. You can use the client to generate the value, but you must make sure that the value is unique among different requests. The token is a string of up to 64 ASCII characters. Enables the reverse replication feature for the replication pairs in a replication pair-consistent group. After you enable the reverse replication feature, the direction of data replication is inverted. Data is replicated from the original secondary disks to the original primary disks. The replication pair-consistent group for which you want to enable reverse replication must be in the **failovered** state. You can call the FailoverDiskReplicaPair operation to enable the failover feature. Before a reverse replication is performed, the primary disks must be detached from the associated ECS instances. You can call the DetachDisk operation to detach disks. After you enable the reverse replication feature, you must call the StartDiskReplicaPairGroup operation again to activate the asynchronous replication feature before data can be replicated from the original secondary disks to the original primary disks.

| SourceRegionId | String | No | cn-beijing | The ID of the region in which the primary site is deployed. |

Disables the asynchronous replication feature for the replication pairs in a replication pair-consistent group. | 404 | InvalidZoneId.NotFound | The specified ZoneId does not exist. | The error message returned because the specified zone ID does not exist. |
| 404 | NoSuchResource | The specified resource does not exist. | The error message returned because the specified resource does not exist. |

| 504 | RequestTimeout | The request is timeout, please try again later. | The error message returned because the request timed out. Try again later. |
|---|---|---|---|
| 500 | InternalError | The request processing has failed due to some unknown error, exception or failure. | The error message returned because an internal error has occurred. |
| 403 | InvalidPayMethod | The specified pay method is not valid. | The error message returned because the billing method is not supported. Check whether the chargeType parameter value is valid. |
| 403 | Forbidden | User is not authorized to operate. | The error message returned because you are not authorized to manage the resource. Check the permissions of your account or contact the administrator of the Apsara Stack tenant account. |
| 403 | Forbidden.Action | User is not authorized to operate this action. | The error message returned because you are not authorized to perform this operation. Check the permissions of your account or contact the administrator of the Apsara Stack tenant account. |
| 403 | NoPermission.SLR | The RAM user does not have the permission to create service linked role: AliyunServiceLinkedRoleForEBS. | The error message returned because you are not authorized to create service-linked roles. |
| 403 | LastTokenProcessing | The last token request is processing. | The error message returned because the token is used in another request that is being processed. Try again later. |
| 403 | InvalidAccountStatus.NotEnough Balance | Your account does not have enough balance. | The error message returned because your account balance is insufficient. |
| 403 | InvalidDiskCategory.NotSupporte d | The specified disk category is not supported. | The error message returned because the specified disk type is not supported by this operation. Check the specified value and view the related topics about API operations for reference. |
| 403 | OperationDenied | The operation is not allowed. | The error message returned because the operation is not supported. |
| 403 | OperationDenied.QuotaExceed | The operation is not allowed due to quota exceed. | The error message returned because the quota for performing this operation has been reached. |
| 403 | NotOnSale.Region | The specified region is not on sale. | The error message returned because requested resources are unavailable for purchase or out of stock in the region. |
| 403 | NotOnSale.Zone | The specified zone is not on sale. | The error message returned because requested resources are unavailable for purchase or out of stock in the zone. |
| 403 | OperationDenied.PairInAnotherGr oup | The operation is not allowed because pair is already in another group. | The error message returned because the replication pair has been added to another replication pair- consistent group and thus the operation is not supported. |
| 403 | OperationDenied.PairNotInGroup | The operation is not allowed because pair is not in any group. | The error message returned because the specified replication pair has not been added to any replication pair-consistent group and thus the operation is not supported. |
| 403 | OperationDenied.NoPairInGroup | The operation is not allowed because no pair in the group. | The error message returned because no replication pairs belong to the specified replication pair- consistent group and thus the operation is not supported. |
| 403 | OperationDenied.PairsExceedInGr oup | The operation is not allowed due to too much pair in the group. | The error message returned because the maximum number of replication pairs in the replication pair- consistent group has been reached and thus the operation is not supported. |

If a request timeout or an internal server error occurs when you call an EBS API operation, the client may resend the request. In this case, you can set the **ClientToken** parameter in the request to prevent the client from repeatedly sending the request.

**What is idempotence**

Idempotence is a property of some operations and resources in mathematics and computer science. Idempotence allows you to obtain the result of the initial request after a request is resent multiple times. Idempotence plays an important role in the distributed system design. In most cases, the client resends a request only when error 500 ( `InternalErrorInternalError` ) or 503 ( `ServiceUnavailable` ) is returned or when no response is received. When you use EBS API, the client generates a parameter value that consists of up to 64 ASCII characters, and you can assign the value to **ClientToken** to ensure the idempotence of the resent requests.

**ClientToken details**

The following section describes the details of **ClientToken**: The **ClientToken** value is a unique and case-sensitive string that is generated by a client and can contain up to 64 ASCII characters in length. Example: `ClientToken=123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426655440000` . If you provide a used value for the **ClientToken** parameter and use different values for other request parameters, the cloud service returns the error code `IdempotentParameterMismatch` .

**Note**

You must use different values for **SignatureNonce**, **Timestamp**, and **Signature** in each retry. This is because ECS uses
**SignatureNonce** to prevent replay attacks and uses **Timestamp** to identify the timestamp of each request. Therefore, you must specify
different **SignatureNonce** and **Timestamp** values in a resent request. Consequently, this changes the value of **Signature**. After you specify the **ClientToken** parameter in a request, the following results may be returned: If the HTTP status code 200 is returned, the client will receive the same result as the last request after the request is resent. However, your server status will not be affected. If an HTTP status code 4xx is returned without the `try it later` error message, a retry will fail. You must troubleshoot issues based on the returned error message before you resend a request.

**Sample idempotent requests**

In this example, the CreateDisk operation is called to create a cloud disk. If you send multiple requests that use the same **ClientToken** value whereas other request parameters remain unchanged, the server returns identical request results with identical **DiskId** values.

```
https://ecs.example.com/?Action=CreateDisk &RegionId=cn-qingdao-env17-d01 &ZoneId=cn-qingdao-env17-amtest11001-a &SnapshotId=s-bp67acfmxazb4p**** &DiskName=test-DiskName &Size=2000 &DiskCategory=cloud_ssd &Description=This is a description example. &Encrypted=false &ClientToken=123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426655440000 &Tag.1.Key=TestKey &Tag.1.Value=TestValue &<Common request parameters>
```

If you do not use **ClientToken**, multiple cloud disks may be created when the client retries operations after errors occur.

**List of operations**

The following section lists some API operations that include **ClientToken** for your reference. For information about whether an API operation includes
**ClientToken**, see the topic that describes the API operation.
This topic describes the API operations and states related to a replication pair.

**API operations**

| API operation | State |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|
|   | Before the operation | If the operation succeeds | If the operation fails |
| CreateDiskReplicaPair | The replication pair does not exist. | created | The operation returns an error, or the replication pair enters the createfailed _ state. |
| StartDiskReplicaPair (Automatic synchronization) | created, initialsyncing, or stopped _ | The replication pair is in the initialsyncing state during the first _ synchronization. Otherwise, the replication pair is in the syncing state. After the synchronization of the current cycle is complete, the replication pair enters the normal state. | The state remains unchanged. |
|   | syncing or normal | The state remains unchanged. | The state remains unchanged. |
| StartDiskReplicaPair (Manual synchronization) | created, manualsyncing, or stopped _ | manualsyncing _ | The state remains unchanged. |

| StopDiskReplicaPair | syncing, initsyncing, manualsyncing, _ _ normal, stopping, stopfailed, or _ stopped | stopped | The state remains unchanged or changes to stopfailed. _ |
|---|---|---|---|
| FailoverDiskReplicaPair | manualsyncing, syncing, normal, _ stopping, stopfailed, stopped, _ failovering, failoverfailed, or _ failovered | failovered | failoverfailed _ |
| ReprotectDiskReplicaPair | failovered, reprotectfailed, or _ reprotecting | stopped | reprotectfailed _ |
| DeleteDiskReplicaPair | created, stopped, invalid, deleted, deletefailed, or deleting _ | The replication pair does not exist. | deletefailed _ |
| ModifyDiskReplicaPair | created or stopped | The state remains unchanged. | The state remains unchanged. |

**States**

| State | Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| creating | Creating | The replication pair is being created. |
| created | Created | The replication pair is created. |
| createfailed _ | Creation Failed | The replication pair cannot be created. We recommend that you delete the replication pair and call the CreateDiskReplicaPair operation again. |
| normal | Normal | The synchronization of the current cycle is complete. |
| initialsyncing _ | Initial Syncing | Data is being synchronized for the first time. |
| manualsyncing _ | One-time Syncing | After data is manually synchronized from the primary disk to the secondary disk, the replication pair returns to the stopped state. If data is manually synchronized from the primary disk to the secondary disk for the first time, the replication pair is in the manualsyncing state during the _ synchronization. |
| syncing | Syncing | Data is being synchronized. |
| invalid | Invalid | The replication pair becomes abnormal due to a user operation. We recommend that you troubleshoot related issues based on the status message. |
| stopping | Stopping | The replication pair is being stopped. |
| stopped | Stopped | The replication pair is stopped. |
| stopfailed _ | Stop Failed | The replication pair cannot be stopped. We recommend that you call the StopDiskReplicaPair operation again. |
| deleting | Deleting | The replication pair is being deleted. |
| deletefailed _ | Deletion Failed | The replication pair cannot be deleted. We recommend that you call the DeleteDiskReplicaPair operation again. |
| deleted | Deleted | The replication pair is deleted. This state is invisible. |
| failovering | In Failover | The failover is being performed. |
| failoverfailed _ | Failover Failed | The failover cannot be performed. We recommend that you call the FailoverDiskReplicaPair operation again. |
| failovered | Failed Over | The failover is complete. |
| reprotecting | In Reverse Replication | The reverse replication is being performed. |
| reprotectfailed _ | Reverse Replication Failed | The reverse replication cannot be performed. We recommend that you call the ReprotectDiskReplicaPair operation again. |

This topic describes how to view the information about API operations. The information includes service names, API operation names, and API versions. The information is required when you use an SDK to call API operations.

AccessKey pairs are classified into AccessKey pairs assigned by Resource Access Management (RAM) and AccessKey pairs assigned by Security Token Service (STS). You can use either type of AccessKey pair for authentication when you call operations. This topic describes how to obtain an AccessKey pair that is assigned by RAM.

**Background information**

An AccessKey pair is used to verify the identity of request senders. An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret that are used to implement symmetric encryption. The AccessKey ID is used to identify a user. The AccessKey secret is used to encrypt the signature string. You can use RAM or STS to assign an AccessKey pair for authentication. Use RAM to assign an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret to a third party. Use STS to assign an AccessKey ID, an AccessKey secret, and a security token to a third party. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides AccessKey pairs for personal accounts or organizations. Only the administrators of level-1 organizations and operations administrators can obtain the AccessKey pairs of organizations. We recommend that you use the AccessKey pairs of personal accounts to call the operations provided by the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and cloud services. If you use the AccessKey pair of a personal account, you must add the following parameters in request headers for access control. If you do not add the parameters, an error may occur. The error indicates that permissions are insufficient.

**Warning**

The AccessKey pair of a personal account is managed by the permission system of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. The AccessKey pair of an organization has more permissions than the AccessKey pair of a personal account. If you want to obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, make sure that you are authorized by an administrator. This helps ensure security.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| x-acs-regionid | The ID of the region. Example: cn-hangzhou-*. |
| x-acs-organizationid | The ID of the organization in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For more information about how to obtain organization IDs, see the GetOrganizationList section in Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Developer Guide. |
| x-acs-resourcegroupid | The ID of the resource set in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For more information about how to obtain resource set IDs, see the ListResourceGroup section in Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Developer Guide. |
| x-acs-instanceid | The ID of the instance on which you want to perform operations. For example, you can obtain the ID of an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance from the ECS instance list. |

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account**

To obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account, perform the following operations:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the upper-right corner of the homepage, move the pointer over the profile picture and click **User Information**.
3. In the **AccessKey Pair** section, view the AccessKey pair of your account.

**Note**

An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. These credentials provide full permissions on cloud resources within your account. You must keep the AccessKey pair confidential.

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization**

To obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, perform the following operations:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Resources > Organizations**.
4. In the organization list, click the name of the level-1 organization whose AccessKey pair you want to obtain.
5. Click **Management Accesskey**.
6. In the dialog box that appears, view the AccessKey pair of the organization.

When you call Apsara Stack operations by using the point of presence (POP) gateway, you must use the SDK of your cloud service. This topic describes how to obtain Alibaba Cloud SDKs. An SDK includes code and examples. You can create cloud applications by using an SDK in the programming language that you require. The SDKs for Java, Python, and Go are provided. You can obtain the SDKs from Alibaba Cloud SDKs based on your business requirements.

**Note**

We recommend that you use an SDK for Java, Python, or Go. If you use SDKs in other programming languages, the SDKs may be incompatible with your system. We recommend that you use the SDK core library that is provided on the Alibaba Cloud official website. The SDK core library is shared by all cloud services and is compatible with Apsara Stack. The following table provides GitHub links to the source code of Log Service SDKs for common programming languages.

| SDK language | Source code on GitHub |
|---|---|
| SDK for Java | Log Service SDK for Java |
| SDK for Python | Log Service SDK for Python |
| SDK for Go | Log Service SDK for Go |
| SDK for PHP | Log Service SDK for PHP |

### 4.2 SDK Reference

Log Service provide software development kits (SDKs) for multiple languages, such as Java, .NET, Python, PHP, and C. You can select an SDK based on your business requirements. Log Service SDKs are implemented based on Log Service APIs. Log Service SDKs provide the same capabilities as Log Service APIs. For more information about Log Service APIs, see API Reference. Before you can use a Log Service SDK, you must have an active Alibaba Cloud AccessKey pair (AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret). In addition, you must specify the endpoint of Log Service in the SDK. For more information, see Basic configurations. Log Service SDKs can be regarded as Log Service APIs that are encapsulated in different languages to provide the following features: Uniform encapsulation. Log Service APIs are uniformly encapsulated. You do not need to create API requests and parse API responses. For more information, see API specifications. The APIs in different languages are similar. This simplifies the switchover between different languages. Automatic digital signatures. You do not need to specify the digital signature logic of Log Service APIs. This simplifies the use of Log Service APIs. Protocol Buffer-formatted encapsulation. The logs collected by Log Service are encapsulated in the Protocol Buffer format. You do not need to specify the format. Automatic compression. Logs are compressed by using the method defined in Log Service APIs. You do not need to manually compress logs. SDKs in some languages allow you to specify whether to write logs in the compression mode. The compression mode is used by default. Centralized error handling methods. You can use SDKs to handle errors based on the relevant language. For more information, see Error handling. Synchronous requests. SDKs in all languages support only synchronous requests. The following table describes the download address and user guide of Log Service SDKs in different languages.

| .NET | .NET SDK and Aliyun.Api.SLS Namespace | GitHub |
| PHP | PHP SDK and SLSPHPSDK _ _ | GitHub |
| Node.js | Node.js SDK | GitHub |
| Python | Python SDK and Python documentation | GitHub |
| C | SDK for C | GitHub |
| GO | SDK for Go | GitHub |
| iOS | iOS SDK | GitHub |
| Android | SDK for Android | GitHub |
| C++ | SDK for C ++ | GitHub |

Before you can use SDKs to interact with Log Service, you must configure the basic settings. This topic describes the basic SDK configurations. Basic configurations: Endpoint: You must specify the endpoint that is used by the client to access Log Service. AccessKey pair (AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret): You must specify the AccessKey pair that is used by the client to access Log Service. The following sections describe how to use endpoints and AccessKey pairs.

**Endpoint**

Before you use an SDK, you must determine the access method and endpoint.
1. When you select an endpoint for a client instance, make sure that the region of your project is the same as the region of your endpoint. Otherwise,
you cannot use the SDK to access your project.
2. All API endpoints support only the HTTP protocol.

**AccessKey pairs**

All interaction requests that are sent to Log Service must be authenticated. An AccessKey pair that consists of an AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret is the critical factor for the authentication. When you create a client instance, you must specify an AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret. You must obtain an AccessKey pair in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Note**

An Apsara Stack tenant account can have multiple AccessKey pairs. You must specify the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret of the same AccessKey pair when you create a client instance. Otherwise, authentication fails. The specified AccessKey must be in the Enabled state. Otherwise, the requests are denied by Log Service. To view the status of the AccessKey pair, you can log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Examples**

Assume that you want to access a project and you have an AccessKey pair that is in the Enabled state. The following AccessKey pair is used:

```
AccessKeyId = "<yourAccessKeyId>" AccessKeySecret = "<yourAccessKeySecret>"
```

This topic describes the basic error handling. SDK errors are classified into the following types: Errors returned by Log Service. This type of errors are handled by SDKs. For more information about this type of errors, see the common error codes of the Log Service API operations. Network errors that occur when you use SDKs to send requests to the server. This type of errors include network disconnection and server response timeout. Errors that are generated by SDKs and are related to platforms or programming languages, for example, memory overflows. All SDKs that are provided by Alibaba Cloud handle errors by throwing exceptions based on the following rules: If the first or second types of errors occur, the SDKs encapsulate the errors as the LogException class and then send the class to users. If the third type of errors occur, the SDKs do not handle the errors but send the errors as the platform-specific and language-specific NativeException class to users.

**LogException**

The LogException class is defined by SDKs to handle the logical errors of Log Service. This class inherits the base class for all exceptions from each language, and provides the following exception information: Error code: indicates the error type. For an error returned by Log Service when you use an SDK, the error code is the same as the error code that is returned by the relevant API operation. The error code for network request errors of SDKs is RequestError. For more information, see API Reference. Error message: indicates the message that is returned together with an error. For an error returned by Log Service when you use an SDK, the error message is the same as the error code that is returned by the relevant API operation. The error message of network errors is "request is failed". For more information, see API Reference. Request ID: indicates the ID of the request for which the current error is returned. The request ID is generated by Log Service. The request ID is returned only when Log Service returns an error message. If Log Service does not return an error message, an empty string is returned. If you receive a request error, you can provide the relevant request ID to the Log Service team for troubleshooting.

**Request failures and retries**

If you use an SDK to access Log Service, the access request may fail due to temporary network disconnection, transmission delay, or slow server response. These errors are thrown as exceptions. Log Service does not implement retry. When you use the SDK, you must customize the handling logic, for example, resend the request or report an error.

SDKs in different languages are implemented in different methods. However, all relevant API operations comply with the request-response principle. These API operations are called by using the following procedure:
1. Create a request instance by using request parameters.
2. Call the corresponding API operation in the SDK and pass the API information to the request instance.
3. Encapsulate the results returned by the SDK interface into a response instance and then return the response instance to the user.
The following snippets show how to obtain the names of all Logstores in a project based on the preceding steps.

Specify the endpoint based on your region and access method. // Create a client instance. Client client = new Client(endpoint, accessId, accessKey); // Specify the project request parameter to initialize the ListLogstores request class. ListLogStoresRequest lsRequest = new ListLogStoresRequest(project); // Use the request instance to call the ListLogstores API operation. The returned parameter is the corresponding response instance. ListLogStoresResponse res = client.ListLogStores(lsRequest); // Access the response instance to retrieve the request results. ArrayList<String> names = res.GetLogStores(); // Other code...
