**Use RAM to authorize a RAM user to access Log Service resources of an Alibaba Cloud account**

You can create projects, Logstores, Logtail configurations, and machine group in Log Service. You have full permissions on these resources. You can call all relevant API operations to use the resources. However, if you use your Alibaba Cloud account to create a RAM user, the RAM user is unauthorized to use your resources in Log Service. To allow the RAM user to use your resources, you must grant relevant permissions on the resources to the RAM user. You can use RAM policies to grant a RAM user the following permissions on Log Service resources: Upload data to a specified Logstore If you grant this permission to a RAM user, the RAM user can upload data to the specified Logstore by using the relevant API or SDK. The policy is as follows: `{`

```json
    "Version": "1",
    "Statement": [
```

`{`

```json
        "Action": [
          "log:Post*",
          "log:BatchPost*"
```

`],`

```json
        "Resource": ["acs:log:*:*:project/<The name of the specified proejct>/logstore/<The name of the specified Logstore>"],
        "Effect": "Allow"
```

`]` Query data of a specified Logstore in the console If you grant this permission to a RAM user, the RAM user can query logs, pull logs, and view the Logstore list after logging on to the Log Service console. The policy is as follows: `{`

```json
    "Version": "1",
    "Statement": [
```

`{`

```json
        "Action": ["log:List*"],
        "Resource": ["acs:log:*:*:project/<The name of the specified proejct>/*"],
        "Effect": "Allow"
```

`},` `{`

```json
        "Action": ["log:Get*"],
        "Resource": ["acs:log:*:*:project/<The name of the proejct>/logstore/<The name of the Logstore>"],
        "Effect": "Allow"
```

`]` You can skip this topic if you do not need to grant access to your Log Service resources across accounts. Skipping this topic does not affect your understanding and use of the other topics in the document. Related topics: This topic describes the resources whose permissions you can grant to a RAM user. You can use an Alibaba Cloud account to grant a RAM user specific permissions on Log Service resources. The following table lists the resources and relevant expressions.

| Resource | Expression in policies |
|---|---|
| Project and Logstore | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/logstore/${logstoreName} |
| Project, Logstore, and LogShipper | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/logstore/${logstoreName}/shipper/${s hipperName} |
|   | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/logstore/* |
| Project and Logtail | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/logtailconfig/${logtailconfig} |
|   | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/logtailconfig/* |
| Project and machine group | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/machinegroup/${machineGroupName } |
|   | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/machinegroup/* |
| Project and consumer group | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/logstore/${logstoreName}/consumerg roup/${consumerGroupName} |
|   | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/logstore/${logstoreName}/consumerg roup/* |
| Project and saved search | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/savedsearch/${savedSearchName} |
|   | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/savedsearch/* |
| Project and dashboard | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/dashboard/${dashboardName} |
|   | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/dashboard/* |
| Project and alert | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/alert/${alarmName} |
|   | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:project/${projectName}/alert/* |
| All types of resources | acs:log:${regionName}:${projectOwnerAliUid}:* |
|   | acs:log:*:${projectOwnerAliUid}:* |

**Note**

The resources in Log Service have hierarchical relationships. Projects are root resources. Logstores, Logtail, and machine groups are parallel sub-resources of projects. LogShipper and consumer groups are sub-resources of Logstores. The following table describes the parameters that are used in policies.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| ${regionName} | The name of a region. |
| ${projectOwnerAliUid} | The ID of an Alibaba Cloud account. |
| ${projectName} | The name of a project. |
| ${logstoreName} | The name of a Logstore. |
| ${logtailconfig} | The name of a Logtail configuration. |
| ${machineGroupName} | The name of a machine group. |
| ${shipperName} | The name of a LogShipper rule. |
| ${consumerGroupName} | The name of a consumer group. |
| ${savedSearchName} | The name of a saved search. |
| ${dashboardName} | The name of a dashboard. |
| ${alarmName} | The name of an alert rule. |

This topic describes the actions that a RAM user can perform on Log Service resources.

**Actions that a RAM user can perform on Log Service resources**

The following table describes the actions that you can authorize a RAM user to perform on Log Service resources.

| Action | Description |
|---|---|
| CreateProject | Creates a project. |
| GetLogs | Queries logs in a Logstore of a specified project. |
| GetHistograms | Queries the distribution of logs in a Logstore of a specified project. |
| GetLogstore | Queries the attributes of a Logstore. |
| ListLogstore | Lists all Logstores in a specified project. |
| CreateLogstore | Creates a Logstore in a project. |
| DeleteLogstore | Deletes a Logstore, including all shards and indexes in the Logstore. |
| UpdateLogstore | Updates the attributes of a Logstore. |
| log:GetCursorOrData(GetCursor and PullLogs) | Queries a cursor based on a specified point in time, and queries logs in a specified shard based on a cursor and the count parameter. |
| ListShards | Lists all available shards in a Logstore. |
| PostLog | Writes log data to a Logstore. |
| CreateConfig | Creates a Logtail configuration in a project. |
| UpdateConfig | Updates a Logtail configuration. |
| DeleteConfig | Deletes a Logtail configuration. |
| GetLogstore | Queries the details of a Logtail configuration. |
| UpdateConfig | Lists all Logtail configurations in a project. You can paginate the configurations by specifying the related parameters. |
| CreateMachineGroup | Creates a machine group to specify the servers from which logs are collected. |
| UpdateMachineGroup | Updates a machine group. |
| DeleteMachineGroup | Deletes a machine group. |
| GetMachineGroup | Queries the details of a machine group. |
| ListMachineGroup | Lists machine groups. |
| ListMachines | Lists the servers in a machine group. The severs are connected to Log Service. |
| ApplyConfigToMachineGroup | Applies a Logtail configuration to a machine group. |
| RemoveConfigFromMachineGroup | Removes a Logtail configuration from a machine group. |
| GetAppliedConfigs | Queries the Logtail configurations that are applied to a specified machine group. |

| CreateConsumerGroup | Creates a consumer group in a specified Logstore. |
|---|---|
| UpdateConsumerGroup | Modifies the attributes of a consumer group. |
| DeleteConsumerGroup | Deletes a specified consumer group. |
| ListConsumerGroup | Lists all consumer groups in a specified Logstore. |
| UpdateCheckPoint | Updates the checkpoint of a shard for a consumer group. |
| HeartBeat | Sends a heartbeat packet to Log Service for a specified consumer. |
| GetCheckPoint | Queries the checkpoints of one or all shards from which a specified consumer group consumes data. |
| CreateIndex | Creates indexes for a specified Logstore. |
| DeleteIndex | Deletes the indexes of a specified Logstore. |
| GetIndex | Queries the indexes of a specified Logstore. |
| UpdateIndex | Updates the indexes of a specified Logstore. |
| log:CreateSavedSearch | Creates a saved search. |
| log:UpdateSavedSearch | Updates a saved search. |
| log:GetSavedSearch | Queries a specified saved search. |
| log:DeleteSavedSearch | Deletes a saved search. |
| log:ListSavedSearch | Lists saved searches. |
| log:CreateDashboard | Creates a dashboard. |
| log:UpdateDashboard | Updates a dashboard. |
| log:GetDashboard | Queries a specified dashboard. |
| log:DeleteDashboard | Deletes a dashboard. |
| log:ListDashboard | Lists dashboards. |
| log:CreateJob | Creates a task, for example, an alert or a subscription. |
| log:UpdateJob | Updates a task. |
| log:CreateApp | Grants a RAM user the permissions to create an application, such as Cost Manager or Log Audit Service. |
| log:UpdateApp | Grants a RAM user the permissions to update an application, such as Cost Manager or Log Audit Service. |
| log:GetApp | Grants a RAM user the permissions to view an application, such as Cost Manager or Log Audit Service. |
| log:DeleteApp | Grants a RAM user the permissions to delete an application, such as Cost Manager or Log Audit Service. |

Log Service allows you to use Key Management Service (KMS) to encrypt data for secure storage. This topic describes the data encryption mechanism of Log Service and how to encrypt data by using KMS.

**Data encryption mechanism**

Log Service encrypts data by using KMS. The data encryption mechanism has the following characteristics: Log Service supports the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) encryption algorithm. You can create and manage a customer master key (CMK) in the KMS console to ensure the security of the CMK. Log Service supports the following encryption types: Service key-based encryption: Log service generates an independent service key for each Logstore. The service key never expires. Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) encryption: You can create a CMK in the KMS console and grant the relevant permissions to Log Service. When Log Service calls a KMS API operation, this CMK is used to create a key for data encryption. If the CMK is deleted or disabled, the BYOK key becomes invalid.

**Important**

You can configure data encryption for a Logstore only when you call the CreateProject operation to create the Logstore. The algorithm or type of data encryption cannot be changed after the Logstore is created. If the CMK created in the KMS console becomes invalid, all read and write requests on the Logstore fail. The CMK generated by the service key of Log Service does not rotate.

**Service key-based encryption**

When you call the CreateProject operation to create a Logstore, add the **encrypt_conf** node to encrypt data by using the following sample code:

```json
encrypt_conf = {
    "enable" : True, # If you set the value to True, data encryption is enabled.
    "encrypt_type": "aes_gcm", # The encryption algorithm. You can set the value tosm4_gcm or aes_gcm.
```

**Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) encryption**

1. In the KMS console, create a BYOK.
For more information, see the **Key Management Service (KMS) > Create a CMK** topic in **User Guide**.
2. Create a level -1 organization.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For more information, see the **User Guide > Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager**
**Management Console** topic.
ii. Creates an organization. For more information, see the **User Guide > Enterprise > Organizations > Create an organization** topic in **User**
**Guide**.
3. Create a RAM role for a level -1 organization.
i. In the top navigation bar of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, click **Configurations**. ii. On the **RAM Service Linked Role** tab, click **Create RAM Role**. iii. In the **Organization Name** drop-down list, select the created organization. In the **Service Name** drop-down list, select **Log Service**, and click
**OK**.
iv. On the **RAM Service Linked Role** page, find the AliyunLogAccessingKMSRole service role, and click **Details** to obtain the ARN of the RAM role.
4. When you call the CreateProject operation to create a Logstore, add the **encrypt_conf** node to encrypt data by using the following sample code:

```json
encrypt_conf = {
    "enable" : True, # If you set the value to True, data encryption is enabled.
    "encrypt_type": "aes_gcm", # The encryption algorithm. You can set the value tosm4_gcm or aes_gcm.
    "user_cmk_info":
```

`{`

```json
            "cmk_key_id": "", # The ID of the CMK that you created in Step 1.
            "arn": "", # The ARN of the RAM role that is obtained in Step 3.
            "region_id" : ""# The ID of the region where the CMK resides.
```

This topic describes the data model of Log Service.

**Project**

A project is a basic management unit in Log Service and is used to isolate and control resources. You can use a project to manage all logs and log sources of an application.

**Logstore**

A Logstore is a unit that collects, stores, and consumes logs in Log Service. Each Logstore belongs to a single project. Each project can have multiple Logstores. You can create multiple Logstores for a project based on your business requirements. We recommend that you create an independent Logstore for each type of logs in an application. For example, you have a game application named big-game. The server stores three types of logs: operation_log, application_log, and access_log. You can create a project named big-game and then create three Logstores in the project to collect, store, and query the three types of logs.

**Log**

A log is the minimum data unit that is processed in Log Service. Log Service uses a semi-structured data model to define a log. The data model is as follows: Topic: a user-defined field that marks multiple logs. For example, access logs can be marked based on the sites. This field is an empty string by default. An empty string is also a valid topic. Time: a reserved field in a log, used to indicate the time when the log is generated. This value is a Unix timestamp representing the number of seconds that have elapsed since the epoch time January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC. Content: a field that records the content of a log. The content consists of one or more content items. Each content item is a key-value pair. Source: a field that indicates the source of a log, for example, the IP address of the machine where the log is generated. This field is empty by default. The following table describes the requirements for the values of these fields. Table 1. Log fields

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| time | An integer in the Unix timestamp format. Unit: seconds. |
| topic | A UTF-8 encoded string of up to 128 characters. |
| source | A UTF-8 encoded string of up to 128 characters. |
| content | One or more key-value pairs. A key is a UTF-8 encoded string of up to 128 characters. It can contain only letters, underscores (), and _ digits. It cannot start with a digit. A value is a UTF-8 encoded string of up to 1,048,576 (1024 × 1024) bytes. |

**Note**

The key in the content field cannot be any of the following keywords: `__time__` , `__source__` , `__topic__` , `__partition_time__` ,

| _extract_others_ |   |
|---|---|

**Topic**

Logs in a Logstore can be grouped by topics. Topics can be specified when you write logs to a Logstore. For example, you can use your user ID as the topic of a log when you write the log to a Logstore. If you do not need to group logs in a Logstore, you can specify the same topic for all logs.

**Note**

An empty string is a valid topic. The topic of a log is an empty string by default. Logs are used in various formats in actual scenarios. The following example shows how to map a raw NGINX access log to the log data model of Log Service. In this example, the IP address of your NGINX server is 10.10.10.1. A raw log on this server is as follows:

```
10.1.1.1 - - [01/Mar/2012:16:12:07 +0800] "GET /Send? AccessKeyId=<yourAccessKeyId> HTTP/1.1" 200 5 "-" "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux i686 on x86_64; rv:10.0.2) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/10.0.2"
```

The following table describes how to map the raw log to the log data model of Log Service. Table 2. Log data model of Log Service

| Field | Field value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| topic | “” | The default value (empty string) is used. |
| time | 1330589527 | The time when the log was generated. The time is converted from the timestamp of the raw log. Unit: seconds. |
| source | “10.10.10.1” | The IP address of the server is used as the log source. |
| content | Key-value pair | The content of the log. |

You can decide how to extract the raw log content and combine the extracted content into key-value pairs. The following table describes custom keyvalue pairs. Table 3. Custom key-value pairs

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| ip | “10.1.1.1” |
| method | “GET” |
| status | “200” |
| length | “5” |
| refurl _ | “-“ |
| browser | “Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux i686 on x8664; rv:10.0.2) Gecko/20100101 Firef _ |

**LogGroup**

A group of logs.

**Logs**

A collection of multiple logs.

**LogGroupList**

A collection of log groups that are used to return results.

**Encoding method**

The following table describes the content encoding method that is supported by Log Service. The RESTful API layer is indicated by Content-Type. Table
4. Supported encoding method

| Encoding method | Content-Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| ProtoBuf | The data model is encoded by Protocol Buffer. | application/x-protobuf |

The following sample code shows how to use Protocol Buffer to define the objects in the data model:

```
message Log
```

`{`

```
    required uint32 Time = 1;// Unix time format
    message Content
```

`{`

```
        required string Key = 1;
        required string Value = 2;
    repeated Content Contents= 2;
message LogGroup
```

`{`

```
    repeated Log Logs= 1;
    optional string Reserved = 2; // Reserved fields
    optional string Topic = 3;
    optional string Source = 4;
message LogGroupList
```

`{`

```
    repeated LogGroup logGroupList = 1;
```

**Note**

When you use the Protocol Buffer format, key-value pairs must be unique. Otherwise, an undefined behavior occurs. Log Service uses Protocol Buffer as the standard log format. You can write logs to Log Service in the Protocol Buffer format. Protocol Buffer is used as a format to interchange structured data. Before you write logs to Log Service by calling relevant API operations, you must serialize raw log data to Protocol Buffer data streams as follows:

```
message Log
```

`{`

```
    required uint32 time = 1; // UNIX Time Format
    message Content
```

`{`

```
        required string key = 1;
        required string value = 2;
    repeated Content contents= 2;
message LogGroup
```

`{`

```
    repeated Log logs= 1;
    optional string reserved =2; // An internal field. You do not need to specify this field.
    optional string topic = 3;
    optional string source = 4;
message LogGroupList
```

`{`

```
    repeated LogGroup logGroupList = 1;
```

**Note**

When you use the Protocol Buffer format, key-value pairs must be unique. Otherwise, an undefined behavior occurs. For more information about the Protocol Buffer format, visit GitHub. For more information about the API operations that write logs to Log Service, see PostLog. A Logstore is a data storage unit. You can create up to 10 Logstores for each project by default. The name of a Logstore must be unique in the project to which the Logstore belongs. A Logstore is the portal for all log data. You can read data from or write data to the Logstore. The naming rules for Logstores are as follows: The name can only contain lowercase letters, digits, hyphens (-), and underscores (_). The name must start and end with a lowercase letter or a digit. The name must be 2 to 63 characters in length. Example `{`

```json
    “logstoreName" : "access_log",
    "ttl": 1,
    "shardCount": 2,
    "createTime":1439538649,
    "lastModifyTime":1439538649
```

The following table describes the Logstore parameters. Table 1. Logstore parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| logstoreName | String | Yes | The name of the Logstore. The name must be unique in the project to which the Logstore belongs. |
|---|---|---|---|
| ttl | Integer | Yes | The time to live (TTL) of log data. Unit: days. Minimum value: 1. |
| shardCount | Integer | Yes | The number of shards in the Logstore. |
| createTime | Integer | No | The time when the Logstore was created in Log Service. This parameter is displayed only in the output result. |
| lastModifyTime | Integer | No | The time when the Logstore is updated in Log Service. This parameter is displayed only in the output result. |

A shard is a basic read/write unit in each Logstore. You can specify the number of shards in each Logstore. To read data from a shard, you must specify the shard. To write data to a shard, you do not need to specify the shard. Instead, you can use the load balancing mode. In this mode, data is written to multiple shards based on automatic balancing. This ensures high availability of the write operation. The following table describes the parameters of a shard. Table 1. Shard parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| shardID | Integer | Yes | The unique ID of a shard in the Logstore. The shard ID is automatically generated by the system. |

You can create up to 100 Logtail configurations for a project. The name of a Logtail configuration must be unique in a project. You can use a Logtail configuration to specify the location, method, and parameters for log collection. The naming rules for Logtail configurations are as follows: The name can only contain lowercase letters, digits, hyphens (-), and underscores (_). The name must start and end with a lowercase letter or a digit. The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length. Example `{`

```json
    "configName": "testcategory1",
    "inputType": "file",
    "inputDetail": {
        "logType": "common_reg_log",
        "logPath": "/var/log/httpd/",
        "filePattern": "access.log",
        "localStorage": true,
        "timeFormat": "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S",
        "logBeginRegex": ".*",
        "regex": "(\w+)(\s+)",
        "key" :[“key1", “key2"],
        "filterKey":["key1"],
        "filterRegex":[“regex1"],
        "topicFormat": “none"
```

`},`

```json
    "outputType": "sls",
    "outputDetail":
```

`{`

```json
        "logstoreName": "perfcounter"
```

`},`

```json
    "createTime": 1400123456,
    "lastModifyTime": 1400123456
```

The following table describes the configuration parameters. Table 1. Configuration parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| configName | String | Yes | The name of the Logtail configuration. The name must be unique in a project. |
| inputType | String | Yes | The input type. Default value: file. |
| inputDetail | json | Yes | See the following table. |
| outputType | String | Yes | The output type. Only LogService is supported. |
| outputDetail | String | Yes | See the following table. |
| createTime | Integer | No | The time when the Logtail configuration was created. |
| lastModifyTime | Integer | No | The time when the Logtail configuration was last updated on Log Service. |

The following table describes the elements of the inputDetail parameter. Table 2. inputDetail elements

| Element | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| logType | String | Yes | The log type. Valid value: commonreglog. _ _ |
| logPath | String | Yes | The parent directory where the log resides, for example, /var/logs/ . |
| filePattern | String | Yes | The pattern of the log file, for example, access*.log . |
| localStorage | Boolean | Yes | Specifies whether to enable the local cache. Logs up to 1 GB can be locally cached when the link to Log Service is disconnected. |
| timeFormat | String | Yes | The format of the log time, for example, %Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S . |
| logBeginRegex | String | Yes | The regular expression that specifies the pattern of the first line of a log. This parameter is applicable to multiline logs. |
| regex | String | Yes | The regular expression that is used to extract logs. |
| key | Array | Yes | The key that is generated after logs are extracted. |
| filterKey | Array | Yes | The key that is used to filter logs. A log meets the requirements only when the key value matches the regular expression specified in the corresponding filterRegex column. |
| filterRegex | Array | Yes | The regular expression that is specified for each filterKey. The length of filterRegex must be the same as that of filterKey. |
| topicFormat | String | No | Specifies part of the log file path as the topic, for example, /var/log/(. *).log . The default value is none, indicating that the topic is null. |
| preserve | Boolean | No | Valid values: true and false. The value true indicates that the directory monitoring never times out. The value false indicates that the timeout period for directory monitoring is 30 minutes. Default value: true. |
| preserveDepth | Integer | No | Specifies the depth of the monitored directories if the preserve parameter is set to false. Maximum value: 3. |

The following table describes the elements of the outputDetail parameter. Table 3. outputDetail elements

| Element | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| logstoreName | String | Yes | The name of the Logstore. |

After a machine with Logtail is started, the machine is automatically associated with the user specified in the Logtail configurations. The machine can be identified by using the following three methods: IP address: the IP address corresponding to the hostname. This is the simplest method, but the IP address may be duplicated in environments such as Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). Universally unique identifier (UUID): the UUID of the desktop management interface (DMI) device. For more information, visit RFC 4122. User-defined ID: the user-defined machine identifier in the Logtail directory. The attributes of each machine are as follows: `{`

```json
    "ip" : "testip1",
    "machine-uniqueid" : "testuuid1",
    "userdefined-id" : "testuserdefinedid1",
    "lastHeartbeatTime”:1397781420
```

The following table describes the machine attribute parameters. Table 1. Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| ip | String | The IP address corresponding to the machine hostname. |
| machine-uniqueid | String | The unique primary key marked by the machine. The primary key is uploaded by Logtail. |
| userdefined-id | String | The user-defined machine identifier that is uploaded by Logtail. |
| lastHeartbeatTime(output-only) | Integer | The last heartbeat time of the machine. The value is a Unix timestamp representing the number of seconds that have elapsed since the epoch time. |

**machinegroup**

The machinegroup parameter indicates the machine group that belongs to the current user in the project. The machine group can be identified by an IP address or user-defined ID. IP addresses are more easily identified than user-defined IDs. However, user-defined IDs can identify machine groups in VPC even when repeated IP addresses exist. You can select either of the two machine identification methods based on your business requirements. The naming rules of machine groups are as follows: The name can contain only lowercase letters, digits, hyphens (-), and underscores (_). The name must start and end with a lowercase letter or digit. The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length.

**Example**

`{`

```json
    "groupName" : "testgroup",
    "groupType" : "",
    "groupAttribute" : {
        "externalName" : "testgroup",
        “groupTopic”: “testgrouptopic”
```

`},`

```json
    “machineIdentifyType”: "ip",
    "machineList" : [
        "ip1",
        "ip2"
        ...
```

`],`

```json
    “createTime”: 1431705075,
    "lastModifyTime" : 1431705075
```

The following table lists the parameters of a machine group. Table 2. Machine group parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| groupName | String | Yes | The name of the machine group. The name must be unique in a project. |
| groupType | String | No | The type of the machine group. Default value: null. |
| machineIdentifyType | String | Yes | The machine identification type. Valid values: ip or userdefined-id. |
| groupAttribute | object | Yes | The attribute of the machine group. Default value: null. |
| machineList | Array | Yes | The list of machine identifiers. Valid values: IP addresses or user-defined identifiers. |
| createTime(output-only) | Integer | No | The time when the machine group was created. |
| lastModifyTime(output-only) | Integer | No | The time when the machine group was last updated on Log Service. |

The following table describes the parameters of groupAttribute. Table 3. groupAttribute parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| groupTopic | String | No | The topic of the machine group. Default value: null. |
| externalName | String | No | The external management identifier on which the machine group depends. Default value: null. |

### 5.1 Preparations

You can log on to the API Tool console from the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Prerequisites**

Before you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, the endpoint of the console is obtained from the deployment personnel. A browser is available. We recommend that you use Google Chrome.

2. Enter your username and password.
Obtain the username and password that are used to log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console from the operations administrator.

**Note**

When you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console for the first time, you must change the password of your account. For security purposes, your password must meet the minimum complexity requirements. The password must be 10 to 32 characters in length and must contain at least two of the following character types: Uppercase or lowercase letters Digits Special characters, which include ! @ # $ %
3. Click **Log On**.
4. If your account has multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled, perform corresponding operations in the following scenarios:
You log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console for the first time after MFA is enabled by the administrator. a. On the Bind Virtual MFA Device page, bind an MFA device. b. Enter the username and password again as in Step 2 and click **Log On**. c. Enter a six-digit MFA verification code and click **Authenticate**. You have enabled MFA and bound an MFA device. Enter a six-digit MFA verification code and click **Authenticate**.

**Note**

For more information, see the **Bind a virtual MFA device to enable MFA** topic in **Apsara Uni-manager Management**
**Console User Guide**.
5. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Others > API Tool**.
This topic describes how to view the information about API operations. Before you use SDKs, you need to obtain service names, API operation names, and API versions.

**Background information**

The API operations on the API Directory page are only for reference. For information about how to call API operations, see developer guide of the corresponding cloud service. If the information on the API Directory page is inconsistent with that in the developer guide of the corresponding cloud service, the information in the developer guide prevails.
1. Log on to the API Tool console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **API Directory**.
3. On the **API Directory** page, select **sgw** from the drop-down list, enter a keyword of an operation name in the search box, and then click Search.
4. View and record the service name, operation name, and API version.
AccessKey credentials are assigned by Resource Access Management (RAM) or Security Token Service (STS). You can use one type of AccessKey credentials for authentication when you call API operations. This topic describes how to obtain an AccessKey pair.

**Background information**

An AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret are used to implement symmetric encryption and verify the identity of request senders. The AccessKey ID is used to identify a user. The AccessKey secret is used to encrypt a signature string. AccessKey credentials can be assigned by RAM or STS: An AccessKey pair that is assigned by RAM to a third party consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. An AccessKey 3-tuple that is assigned by STS to a third party consists of an AccessKey ID, an AccessKey secret, and a security token. For more information, see Obtain an STS AccessKey 3-tuple. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides AccessKey pairs for personal accounts or organizations. Only the administrators of level-1 organizations and operations administrators can obtain the AccessKey pairs of organizations. We recommend that you use the AccessKey pairs of personal accounts to call the operations provided by the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and cloud services. If you use the AccessKey pair of a personal account, configure the header parameters that are described in the following table for access control. Otherwise, an error that indicates insufficient permissions can occur.

**Warning**

The AccessKey pair of a personal account is managed and controlled by the permission system of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. If you need to obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, make sure that your operation is allowed by an administrator. This ensures security.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| x-acs-regionid | The ID of the region. Example: cn-hangzhou-*. |

| x-acs-organizationid | The ID of the organization in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For information about how to obtain an organization ID, see the "GetOrganizationList" section in Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Developer Guide. |
|---|---|
| x-acs-resourcegroupid | The ID of the resource set in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For information about how to obtain a resource set ID, see the "ListResourceGroup" section in Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Developer Guide. |
| x-acs-instanceid | The ID of the instance that you want to manage. If you want to obtain the ID of an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance, you can obtain the ID from the ECS instance list. |

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account**

To obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account, perform the following steps:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. Click the profile picture in the upper-right corner of the page and click **User Information**.
3. In the **AccessKey Pair** section, view the AccessKey pair of the personal account.

**Note**

An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. These credentials provide full permissions on cloud resources within your account. You must keep the AccessKey pair confidential.

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization**

To obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, perform the following steps:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Resources > Organizations**.
4. In the organization list, click the name of the level-1 organization whose AccessKey pair you want to obtain.
5. Click **Management AccessKey** on the right side of the page.
6. In the dialog box that appears, view the AccessKey pair of the organization.
This topic describes how to use STS to call API operations in Apsara Stack.

**Background information**

STS allows you to use temporary credentials to access Apsara Stack resources. You can use STS to call API operations in Apsara Stack. An STS AccessKey 3-tuple consists of an AccessKey ID, an AccessKey secret, and a security token. When you use STS to call API operations, you must specify an STS AccessKey 3-tuple.

**Procedure**

1. Obtain the Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of your `RAM role` .
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. ii. In the upper-right corner of the homepage, click the profile picture and click **User Information**. iii. Click **View Current Role Policy**. In the **View Policies of Current Role** dialog box, view the ARN of your `RAM role` .
2. Obtain the STS AccessKey 3-tuple.

**Note**

In the following sample code, replace the parameters with the actual information. Delete the angle brackets (<>) in the final code. The following section describes the parameters: <yourRegionID>: Replace the parameter with the region ID. <yourAccessKeyID>: Replace the parameter with your AccessKey ID. <yourAccessKeySecret>: Replace the parameter with your AccessKey secret. <yourRoleSessionName>: Replace the parameter with the name of the current session. <yourRoleArn>: Replace the parameter with the ARN of your RAM role. "sts.aliyuns.com": Replace the parameter with the endpoint of STS.

```java
public static void main(String[] args) {
    // Create and initialize a DefaultAcsClient instance.
    // Specify the region ID, AccessKey ID, and AccessKey secret.
    DefaultProfile profile = DefaultProfile.getProfile("<yourRegionID>", "<yourAccessKeyID>", "<yourAccessKeySecret>");
    HttpClientConfig clientConfig = HttpClientConfig.getDefault();
    clientConfig.setIgnoreSSLCerts(true);
    clientConfig.setProtocolType(ProtocolType.HTTPS);
    profile.setHttpClientConfig(clientConfig);
    IAcsClient client = new DefaultAcsClient(profile);
    String assumeRole = callAssumeRole(client);
    if (StringUtils.isEmpty(assumeRole)) return;
    JSONObject assumeRoleJson = JSONObject.parseObject(assumeRole);
    JSONObject credentials = assumeRoleJson.getJSONObject("Credentials");
    // Obtain the STS AccessKey 3-tuple.
    String stsAK = credentials.getString("AccessKeyId");
    String stsSK = credentials.getString("AccessKeySecret");
    String stsToken = credentials.getString("SecurityToken");
private static String callAssumeRole(IAcsClient client) {
    CommonRequest request = new CommonRequest();
    // Replace sts.aliyuns.com with the endpoint of STS. The format of an STS endpoint is sts-vpc.${global:region}.${global:internet-
domain}.
    request.setSysDomain("sts.aliyuns.com");
    request.setSysProduct("Sts");
    request.setSysAction("AssumeRole");
    request.setSysVersion("2015-04-01");
    request.setSysMethod(MethodType.POST);
    request.setHttpContentType(FormatType.FORM);
    // Replace <yourRoleSessionName> with the name of the current session.
    request.putQueryParameter("RoleSessionName", "<yourRoleSessionName>");
    // Replace <yourRoleArn> with the ARN of the RAM role that you obtain in the preceding step.
    request.putQueryParameter("RoleArn", "<yourRoleArn>");
    try {
        CommonResponse response = client.getCommonResponse(request);
        return response.getData();
    } catch (ServerException e) {
        System.out.println(e.getErrCode());
        System.out.println(e.getErrMsg());
    } catch (ClientException e) {
        System.out.println(e.getErrCode());
        System.out.println(e.getErrMsg());
    return null;
```

You must set header parameters when you call API operations. This topic describes the header parameters and how to obtain the values of the parameters. This topic also describes the return values of some parameters after you call API operations.

**Header parameters**

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| x-acs-regionid | The ID of the region. For more information about how to obtain region IDs, see Obtain a region ID. |
| x-acs-organizationid | The ID of the organization in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For more information about how to obtain organization IDs, see Obtain an organization ID. |
| x-acs-resourcegroupid | The ID of the resource set in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. For more information about how to obtain resource set IDs, see Obtain a resource set ID. |
| x-acs-instanceid | The ID of the gateway on which you want to perform operations. For more information about how to obtain gateway IDs, see Obtain a gateway ID. |

**Query a region ID**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Resources** > **Regions**.
4. Click the name of the organization that you want to view.
5. View the region ID in the **Regions** section on the right.

**Obtain an organization ID**

You must call an API operation to obtain an organization ID. For more information about how to obtain organization IDs, see the GetOrganizationList section in Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Developer Guide.

**Obtain a resource set ID**

You must call an API operation to obtain a resource set ID. For more information about how to obtain resource set IDs, see the ListResourceGroup section in Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Developer Guide.

**Obtain a gateway ID**

You can obtain the ID of a gateway in the cloud service console of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Perform the following operations to obtain a gateway ID:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Storage** > **Object Storage Service** .
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Cloud Storage Gateways**.
4. On the Cloud Storage Gateways page, view the **gateway ID**.

**Response parameters**

The following response parameters are returned by default when you call operations to query the instances of cloud services.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| ResourceGroupName | The name of the resource set. |
| ResourceGroup | The ID of the resource set. |
| DepartmentName | The name of the organization. |
| Department | The ID of the organization. |

This topic describes how to obtain the endpoint of VPN Gateway.

**Background information**

To use the POP gateway to call API operations in Apsara Stack, you must specify the endpoint of a cloud service. You can obtain service endpoints from Apsara Stack onsite O&M engineers. You can also perform the following steps to obtain an endpoint.

icon next to **Service** to search for `csg-controller` .

This topic describes how to use Cloud Storage Gateway (CSG) SDK for Java to initiate a request.
1. Create an AcsClient instance.

```
IAcsClient client = new DefaultAcsClient(profile);
```

2. Create a request.
The naming convention for the Request class is ${apiName}Request , where **${apiName}** indicates the API name, such as DescribeGateways. When multiple service SDKs are used, different requests may have the same name. You can differentiate the requests based on package names.

```
DescribeGatewaysRequest request = new DescribeGatewaysRequest(); // Configure service-related parameters. request.setPageSize(10); request.setPageNumber(1);
```

3. Initiate the request and handle the response.

| DescribeGatewaysResponse response; try { response = client.getAcsResponse(request); for (DescribeGatewaysResponse.Gateway gateway:response.getGateways()) { System.out.println(gateway.getGatewayId()); } } catch (ServerException e) { e.printStackTrace(); } catch (ClientException e) { e.printStackTrace(); } |   |   |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| In normal cases, all returned fields are deserialized into the response. You can directly use |   |   | response.getXXX() | to obtain the response fields. |
| String name = response.getName() |   |   |   |   |
| If an exception occurs or you need to check the original HTTP response, use | doAction() | to obtain the original response. |   |   |
| HttpResponse response = client.doAction(request); |   |   |   |   |

This topic describes how to handle the errors of Cloud Storage Gateway (CSG) SDK for Java. If the server or SDK encounters an error when you use CSG SDK for Java, it returns an error response. The error response contains an error code and an error message. In most cases, you do not need to handle the errors returned by CSG SDK for Python. You only need to handle the errors returned by the server based on error messages. `ServerException` indicates a server error. `ClientException` indicates an SDK error. For example, when the following error occurs, you can modify the AccessKey ID based on the error message to solve the problem:

```
 com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ClientException: InvalidAccessKeyId.NotFound : Specified access key is not found.
```

If you want to handle the SDK errors returned by CSG SDK for Java, refer to the following example to write your code:

```java
try { FooResponse response = client.getAcsResponse(request); // Handle the response. //... }catch (ServerException e){ // You can add your own error handling logic here. // For example, print the error message. System.out.println("ErrorCode=" + e.getErrCode()); System.out.println("ErrorMessage=" + e.getErrMsg()); // If you are unable to troubleshoot the problem, submit a ticket and provide RequestId to Alibaba Cloud technical support. System.out.println("ResponseId=" + e.getRequestId()); }catch (ClientException e){ // You can add your own error handling logic here. // For example, print the error message. System.out.println("ErrorCode=" + e.getErrCode()); System.out.println("ErrorMessage=" + e.getErrMsg());
```

### 5.3 Call examples of SDK for Python

This topic describes how to obtain and use CSG SDK for Python.

**Prerequisites**

An Apsara Stack tenant account that has the required permissions and an AccessKey pair that consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret are obtained. For more information, see . The endpoint of CSG is obtained. For more information, see Obtain the endpoint of Cloud Storage Gateway.
1. Install the core library of Alibaba Cloud SDK.
If you use Python 2.x, run the following command to install the core library:

```
pip install aliyun-python-sdk-core
```

If you use Python 3.x, run the following command to install the core library:

```
pip3 install aliyun-python-sdk-core-v3
```

Before you install CSG SDK for Python, you must download the SDK package. For more information, see Obtain Cloud Storage Gateway SDKs. If you use Python 2.x, decompress the SDK package and run the following command to install the SDK:

```
python setup.py install
```

If you use Python 3.x, decompress the SDK package and run the following command to install the SDK:

```
python3 setup.py install
```

To use CSG SDK for Python, perform the following steps:
1. Create a client instance. When you create a client instance, you must specify a region ID, an AccessKey ID, and an AccessKey secret.
2. Create an API request and set the required parameters.
3. Initiate the API request and process the response or exception.

**Note**

In the following sample code, replace the parameters with the actual information. Delete the angle brackets (<>) in the final code. The following section describes the parameters: <yourRegionID>: Replace the parameter with the region ID. <yourAccessKeyID>: Replace the parameter with your AccessKey ID. <yourAccessKeySecret>: Replace the parameter with your AccessKey secret. <sgw.aliyuns.com>: Replace the parameter with the endpoint of CSG.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python
# coding=utf-8
from aliyunsdkcore import client from aliyunsdkcore.profile import region_provider from aliyunsdksgwhybrid.request.v20180511 import DescribeGatewaysRequest
# global config
region_id = '<yourRegionID>' # Replace the parameter with the region ID. access_key = '<yourAccessKeyID>' # Replace the parameter with your AccessKey ID. acces_secret = '<yourAccessKeySecret>' # Replace the parameter with your AccessKey secret.
# product config
product_name = 'sgw' # Specify the service name. endpoint = '<sgw.aliyuns.com>' # Replace the parameter with the endpoint of CSG.
# create client
region_provider.modify_point(product_name, region_id, endpoint) clt = client.AcsClient(access_key, acces_secret, region_id)
# setup request
request = DescribeGatewaysRequest.DescribeGatewaysRequest() request.set_endpoint(endpoint) request.set_content_type("application/json") request.set_accept_format("JSON")
# get response
response = clt.do_action_with_exception(request) print(response)
```

```
clt = client.AcsClient(secret_id, secret_key, region_id)
```

Apsara Stack SDK for Python allows you to initiate API requests over HTTP and HTTPS. You can specify a protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) for a specific request, or set a global default protocol.

**Note**

The default protocol of the service takes precedence over the global default protocol.

**Add OpenSSL support**

The HTTPS protocol support of Apsara Stack SDK for Python is based on the OpenSSL support in Python. To use Apsara Stack SDK for Python to make requests over HTTPS, you need to add OpenSSL support in Python. OpenSSL supports TLS 1.2 or later.

| Run the | python -c "import ssl" | c |
|---|---|---|
| ImportError: No module named ssl |   |   |

Run the `python -c "import ssl"` command to check whether OpenSSL is supported in Python. If `ImportError: No module named ssl` is not displayed in the command output, OpenSSL is already supported. If OpenSSL is not supported, run the following command to install it:

```
pip install pyopenssl
```

**Example: Set the protocol type of a request to HTTPS.**

The following code shows how to set HTTPS as the protocol for a request:

```bash
request = DescribeGatewaysRequest.DescribeGatewaysRequest() request.set_protocol_type("https")
# Valid value: https or http
```

**Example: Set a global default protocol.**

The following code shows how to set a global protocol for all service requests:

```java
import aliyunsdkcore.request aliyunsdkcore.request.set_default_protocol_type("https")
# Create a request and call client.do_action_with_exception() to send the request.
```

This topic describes how to use Cloud Storage Gateway (CSG) SDK for Python to initiate a request.

**Procedure**

1. Install CSG SDK

```python
from aliyunsdkcore import client from aliyunsdkcore.profile import region_provider from aliyunsdksgwhybrid.request.v20180511 import DescribeGatewaysRequest
```

2. Create an AcsClient instance.

```
client.region_provider.modify_point(product_name, region_id, endpoint) clt = client.AcsClient(access_key, access_secret, region_id)
```

3. Create a request object.

```
request = DescribeGatewaysRequest.DescribeGatewaysRequest() request.set_endpoint(endpoint) request.set_content_type("application/json") request.set_accept_format("JSON")
```

4. Initiate the request and process the response.

```
response = clt.do_action_with_exception(request) print response
```

If the server or SDK encounters an error when you use CSG SDK for Python, it returns an error response. The error response contains an error code and an error message. In most cases, you do not need to handle the errors returned by CSG SDK for Python. You only need to handle the errors returned by the server based on error messages. `ServerException` indicates a server error. `ClientException` indicates an SDK error. For example, when the following error occurs, you can modify the AccessKey ID based on the error message to solve the problem:

```
aliyunsdkcore.acs\_exception.exceptions.ServerException: HTTP Status: 404 Error:InvalidAccessKeyId.NotFound Specified access key is not found.
```

If you want to handle the SDK errors returned by CSG SDK for Python, refer to the following example to write your code:

```bash
try:
    response = client.do_action_with_exception(request)
except ServerException as e:
    # You can add your own error handling logic here.
    # For example, display the error message.
    print e.get_http_status()
    print e.get_error_code()
    print e.get_error_msg()
```

### 5.4 API reference

The following tables describe the API operations that you can call in CSG. Table 1. Gateway

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| CreateGateway | Creates a gateway. |
| DescribeGateways | Queries the information about gateways. |
| DescribeGateway | Queries the basic information about a gateway. |
| ModifyGateway | Modifies the basic information about a gateway. |
| DeleteGateway | Deletes a gateway. |
| UpgradeGateway | Upgrades a gateway. |
| RebootGateway | Restarts a gateway. |
| DescribeTasks | Queries the information about tasks. |

Table 2. Share

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| DeployCacheDisk | Creates a share. |
| DescribeGatewayFileShares | Queries the configuration information about the shares for a gateway. |
| ModifyGatewayFileShare | Modifies a share. |
| DeleteGatewayFileShares | Deletes a share from a gateway. |
| CreateGatewaySMBUser | Adds a Server Message Block (SMB) user to a gateway. |
| DescribeGatewaySMBUsers | Queries the SMB users of a gateway. |
| DeleteGatewaySMBUser | Removes an SMB user from a gateway. |

Table 3. Cache disk

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| DescribeGatewayCaches | Queries the information about cache disks. |
| ExpandCacheDisk | Scales up a cache disk for a gateway. |
| DeleteGatewayCacheDisk | Deletes a cache disk from a gateway. |

**Common request parameters**

Common parameters are required in all Cloud Storage Gateway (CSG) API requests. Table 1. Common request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Format | String | No | The type of the returned value. Valid value: JSON. |
| Version | String | Yes | The version number of the API. Specify the version number in the YYYY-MM-DD format. Example: 2019-05- 10. |
| AccessKeyId | String | Yes | The AccessKey ID provided to you by Apsara Stack. |

| AccessKeySecret | String | Yes | The AccessKey secret provided to you by Apsara Stack. |
|---|---|---|---|
| RegionId | String | Yes | The region ID provided to you by Apsara Stack. |
| Product | String | Yes | The name of the service. Set the value to sgw. |

You can obtain the values of the `Product` and `Version` parameters in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Perform the following steps:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Others > API Tool**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **API Directory**.
4. In the **Operation Name** search box, enter the name of an operation to query its information.
